title.zh: 卷五十四 列傳第三十五 高逸
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第三十五 高逸 Volume 54 Biographies 35: Hermits

sentences.zh: 南齊書卷五十四‧列傳第三十五 高逸

translations.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 54, Biography 35: Hermits
translations.idiomatic: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 54, Biography 35: Hermits

sentences.zh: 《易》有君子之道四焉，語默之謂也。

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says the Way of the gentleman has four aspects—this is what is meant by speech and silence.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi speaks of four aspects of the gentleman's Way—by which is meant when to speak and when to remain silent.

sentences.zh: 故有入廟堂而不出，徇江湖而永歸。

translations.literal: Therefore some enter the temple hall and never leave; others follow rivers and lakes and return forever.
translations.idiomatic: Some thus enter the halls of government and never depart; others heed the call of lakes and rivers and withdraw for good.

sentences.zh: 隱避紛紜，情迹萬品。

translations.literal: In hiding from worldly tumult, sentiments and traces take countless forms.
translations.idiomatic: In retreat from the world's turmoil, temperament and conduct take endless variety.

sentences.zh: 若道義內足，希微兩亡，藏景窮巖，蔽名愚谷，解桎梏於仁義，永形神於天壤，則名教之外，別有風猷。

translations.literal: If inner sufficiency in the Way and virtue makes one indifferent to fame and obscurity alike, hiding one's light in rugged cliffs and concealing one's name in foolish valleys, releasing oneself from the shackles of benevolence and righteousness and perpetuating body and spirit in heaven and earth—then beyond the teachings of names and principles there exists a distinctive ethos.
translations.idiomatic: When one is inwardly complete in the Way and virtue, untroubled by fame or obscurity, dwelling in remote crags under an assumed name in forgotten valleys, freed from the bonds of conventional morality and at one with heaven and earth—then outside the orthodox teaching there flourishes a spirit all its own.

sentences.zh: 故堯封有非聖之人，孔門謬雞黍之客。

translations.literal: Therefore Yao's fief held men who were not sages; Confucius's gate wrongly admitted a guest bearing millet and chicken.
translations.idiomatic: Even Yao's domain sheltered men who were no sages; even Confucius's school once misjudged a visitor bearing simple fare.

sentences.zh: 次則揭獨往之高節，重去就之虛名，激競違貪，與世爲異。

translations.literal: Next are those who proclaim the lofty integrity of walking alone, who prize the empty fame of departure and return, who stir competition and reject greed, differing from the world.
translations.idiomatic: Next come those who tout the noble resolve to go their own way, who care overly much for the reputation of coming and going, who scorn the race for gain and set themselves apart from society.

sentences.zh: 或慮全後悔，事歸知殆；

translations.literal: Some fear that complete safety will lead to later regret, and affairs return to awareness of danger;
translations.idiomatic: Some, fearing that security will breed remorse, keep watch for peril in every turn of events;

sentences.zh: 或道有不申，行吟山澤。

translations.literal: some have the Way unfulfilled and walk singing through mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: others find the Way blocked and wander the hills and waters chanting their laments.

sentences.zh: 咸皆用宇宙而成心，借風雲以爲戒。

translations.literal: All take the cosmos to complete their minds and borrow wind and clouds as warnings.
translations.idiomatic: All alike take the universe as the measure of their hearts and read wind and cloud as portents to heed.

sentences.zh: 果志達道，未或非然。

translations.literal: If the will is truly fulfilled and the Way attained, this may not be wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Where resolve is genuine and the Way is reached, such lives are hardly to be faulted.

sentences.zh: 含貞養素，文以藝業。

translations.literal: To embrace purity and cultivate simplicity, adorning with literary and artistic accomplishment—
translations.idiomatic: To hold fast to integrity and nourish simplicity, lending grace through learning and art—

sentences.zh: 不然，與樵者之在山，何殊別哉？

translations.literal: otherwise, how would they differ from woodcutters in the mountains?
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, what would separate them from common woodcutters in the hills?

sentences.zh: 故樊英就徵，不稱李固之望；

translations.literal: Therefore when Fan Ying accepted summons, he did not live up to Li Gu's hopes;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Ying answered the call to office and failed Li Gu's expectations;

sentences.zh: 馮恢下節，見陋張華之語。

translations.literal: Feng Hui lowered his standards and was slighted in Zhang Hua's words.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Hui compromised his principles and earned Zhang Hua's contempt.

sentences.zh: 期之塵外，庶以弘多。

translations.literal: Expecting them to dwell beyond the dust, one may broadly extend the account.
translations.idiomatic: Looking to those who dwell beyond the world's dust, one hopes thereby to broaden the record.

sentences.zh: 若今十餘子者，仕不求聞，退不譏俗，全身幽履，服道儒門，斯逸民之軌操，故綴爲《高逸篇》云爾。

translations.literal: As for the more than ten men of today, in office they do not seek renown, in retirement they do not scorn the vulgar; they preserve themselves in secluded conduct and follow the Way within the Confucian school—these are the norms and conduct of withdrawn men; therefore they are compiled in the "Hermits" chapter, thus.
translations.idiomatic: The dozen or so figures treated here sought no fame in serving office and showed no disdain for common folk in withdrawal; they kept body and spirit whole in seclusion while honoring the Confucian Way—the very measure of the true recluse. Hence they are gathered in this chapter on Hermits.

sentences.zh: 褚伯玉

translations.literal: Chu Boyu
translations.idiomatic: Chu Boyu

sentences.zh: 褚伯玉字元璩，吳郡錢唐人也。

translations.literal: Chu Boyu, styled Yuanzhang, was a native of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Boyu, courtesy name Yuanzhang, came from Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖含，始平太守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Han was Administrator of Shiping.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Han served as Administrator of Shiping.

sentences.zh: 父逷，征虜參軍。

translations.literal: His father Ti was a staff officer under the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ti was a staff officer in the campaign against the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 伯玉少有隱操，寡嗜欲。

translations.literal: Boyu from youth had a disposition for withdrawal and few desires.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Boyu was drawn to seclusion and had few worldly appetites.

sentences.zh: 年十八，父爲之婚，婦入前門，伯玉從後門出。

translations.literal: At age eighteen his father arranged a marriage for him; when the bride entered the front gate, Boyu went out the back gate.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen his father arranged his marriage; as the bride came in the front door, Boyu slipped out the back.

sentences.zh: 遂往剡，居瀑布山。

translations.literal: He then went to Shan and dwelt on Waterfall Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: He made his way to Shan and settled on Waterfall Mountain.

sentences.zh: 性耐寒暑，時人比之王仲都。

translations.literal: By nature he endured cold and heat; men of the time compared him to Wang Zhongdu.
translations.idiomatic: He bore extremes of cold and heat easily; contemporaries likened him to Wang Zhongdu.

sentences.zh: 在山三十餘年，隔絕人物。

translations.literal: For more than thirty years on the mountain he was cut off from human contact.
translations.idiomatic: For over thirty years on the mountain he lived apart from the world of men.

sentences.zh: 王僧達爲吳郡，苦禮致之，伯玉不得已，停郡信宿，裁交數言而退。

translations.literal: When Wang Sengda was magistrate of Wu, he earnestly invited Boyu with courtesy; Boyu had no choice but to stay in the commandery for a night or two, exchanged only a few words, and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Sengda became governor of Wu, he pressed his invitation with elaborate courtesy; Boyu reluctantly stayed a night or two in the prefectural seat, spoke barely a few words, and left.

sentences.zh: 寧朔將軍丘珍孫與僧達書曰：「聞褚先生出居貴館，此子滅景雲棲，不事王侯，抗高木食，有年載矣。

translations.literal: General Ning-Shuo Qiu Zhensun wrote to Sengda: "I hear that Master Chu has come out to lodge in your honored residence. This man has hidden his light and dwelt among clouds, not serving kings and marquises, defying heights and living on tree food, for many years now.
translations.idiomatic: General Ning-Shuo Qiu Zhensun wrote to Sengda: "I hear that Master Chu has emerged to stay at your distinguished residence. For years this man has hidden his brilliance among the clouds, refused the service of kings and lords, lived aloft on trees and fed on their bounty.

sentences.zh: 自非折節好賢，何以致之。

translations.literal: Unless one bends one's will to esteem the worthy, how could one bring this about?
translations.idiomatic: Unless you humbled yourself to honor the worthy, how could you have drawn him here?

sentences.zh: 昔文舉棲冶城，安道入昌門，於茲而三焉。

translations.literal: In the past Wenju dwelt at Ye Castle and Andao entered Chang Gate—now this makes three such cases.
translations.idiomatic: Once Kong Rong sheltered at Ye Castle and Dai Andao entered Chang Gate—now yours makes a third.

sentences.zh: 夫却粒之士，飡霞之人，乃可蹔致，不宜久羈。

translations.literal: Men who reject grain and dine on mist may be summoned briefly; they should not be detained long.
translations.idiomatic: Men who live without grain and feast on cloud-mist may be hosted briefly—they should not be held long.

sentences.zh: 君當思遂其高步，成其羽化。

translations.literal: You should think to let him complete his lofty course and achieve his transformation to immortality.
translations.idiomatic: You should release him to resume his lofty path and fulfill his ascent to transcendence.

sentences.zh: 望其還策之日，蹔紆清塵，亦願助爲譬說。

translations.literal: When he returns to mount his carriage, if you would briefly lay aside pure dust, I also wish to help in offering explanation.
translations.idiomatic: If on the day he departs you would briefly set aside worldly cares, I too would gladly help persuade him.

sentences.zh: 」僧達答曰：「褚先生從白雲遊舊矣。

translations.literal: " Sengda replied: "Master Chu has long wandered with white clouds.
translations.idiomatic: " Sengda replied: "Master Chu has long roamed with the white clouds.

sentences.zh: 古之逸民，或留慮兒女，或使華陰成市，而此子索然，唯朋松石。

translations.literal: Hermits of old sometimes kept concern for sons and daughters, or made Huayin into a market town, but this man is utterly bare, having only pines and rocks as companions.
translations.idiomatic: Recluses of antiquity sometimes still fretted over their children, or drew crowds until Huayin became a marketplace; this man is utterly spare, with only pines and stones for company.

sentences.zh: 介於孤峰絕嶺者，積數十載。

translations.literal: Dwelling among lone peaks and sheer ridges, he has accumulated several decades.
translations.idiomatic: He has lived among solitary peaks and sheer ridges for decades on end.

sentences.zh: 近故要其來此，冀慰日夜。

translations.literal: Recently I therefore invited him here, hoping to ease day and night.
translations.idiomatic: I recently invited him here in the hope of easing my longing day and night.

sentences.zh: 比談討芝桂，借訪荔蘿，若已窺煙液，臨滄洲矣。

translations.literal: Just now in discussing iris and cassia and borrowing talk of creepers and vines, it is as if I have already glimpsed the misty waters and stood before the green isles.
translations.idiomatic: In our talk of fragrant herbs and mountain vines I feel as though I have already glimpsed the misty depths and stood on the shores of the blue isles.

sentences.zh: 知君欲見之，輙當申譬。」

translations.literal: Knowing that you wish to see him, I shall at once offer explanation."
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that you wish to see him, I shall convey your message at once."

sentences.zh: 明僧紹

translations.literal: Ming Sengshao
translations.idiomatic: Ming Sengshao

sentences.zh: 明僧紹字承烈，平原鬲人也。

translations.literal: Ming Sengshao, styled Chenglie, was a native of Ge in Pingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Sengshao, courtesy name Chenglie, came from Ge in Pingyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖玩，州治中。

translations.literal: His grandfather Wan was a commandery aide.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Wan served as a commandery aide.

sentences.zh: 父略，給事中。

translations.literal: His father Lue was a Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lue held the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 僧紹宋元嘉中再舉秀才，明經有儒術。

translations.literal: Sengshao twice passed the xiucai examination in the Yuanjia era of Song and was versed in the classics with Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanjia reign of Liu Song, Sengshao twice passed the provincial examination and was accomplished in the classics and Confucian learning.

sentences.zh: 永光中，鎮北府辟功曹，竝不就。

translations.literal: In the Yongguang era the Northern Defense headquarters summoned him as Registrar, but he did not accept either post.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongguang the Northern Defense headquarters offered him the post of Registrar; he declined both appointments.

sentences.zh: 隱長廣郡嶗山，聚徒立學。

translations.literal: He withdrew to Mount Lao in Changguang Commandery, gathered disciples, and established a school.
translations.idiomatic: He retired to Mount Lao in Changguang Commandery, gathered students, and founded a school.

sentences.zh: 淮北沒虜，乃南渡江。

translations.literal: When north of the Huai fell to the barbarians, he crossed the river south.
translations.idiomatic: When the north bank of the Huai fell to the invaders, he crossed the Yangzi to the south.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始六年，徵通直郎，不就。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Taishi under Emperor Ming he was summoned as Attendant of Direct Communication but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Taishi, Emperor Ming summoned him as Attendant of Direct Communication; he declined.

sentences.zh: 慶符罷任，僧紹隨歸，住江乘攝山。

translations.literal: When Qingfu left office, Sengshao followed him home and dwelt on Mount She in Jiangcheng.
translations.idiomatic: When Qingfu left his post, Sengshao accompanied him and settled on Mount She in Jiangcheng.

sentences.zh: 太祖謂慶符曰：「卿兄高尚其事，亦堯之外臣。

translations.literal: The founder said to Qingfu: "Your elder brother elevates his affairs—he is also an outer minister of Yao.
translations.idiomatic: The founder said to Qingfu: "Your elder brother holds himself aloof in high principle—he is like one of Yao's ministers beyond the court.

sentences.zh: 朕雖不相接，有時通夢。

translations.literal: Though We have no direct contact, at times We communicate in dreams.
translations.idiomatic: Though I have no direct dealings with him, at times we meet in dreams.

sentences.zh: 」遺僧紹竹根如意，筍籜冠。

translations.literal: " He sent Sengshao a ruyi scepter of bamboo root and a hat of bamboo sheaths.
translations.idiomatic: " He sent Sengshao a ruyi scepter carved from bamboo root and a hat woven from bamboo sheaths.

sentences.zh: 僧紹聞沙門釋僧遠風德，往候定林寺，太祖欲出寺見之。

translations.literal: Sengshao heard of the moral stature of the monk Shi Sengyuan and went to call on him at Dinglin Temple; the founder wished to leave the temple to see him.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing of the monk Shi Sengyuan's moral stature, Sengshao went to visit him at Dinglin Temple; the founder wished to go out to the temple to see him.

sentences.zh: 僧遠問僧紹曰：「天子若來，居士若爲相對？

translations.literal: Sengyuan asked Sengshao: "If the Son of Heaven comes, how will the gentleman receive him?
translations.idiomatic: Sengyuan asked Sengshao: "If the emperor comes, how will you receive him?

sentences.zh: 」僧紹曰：「山藪之人，政當鑿坏以遁，若辭不獲命，便當依戴公故事耳。

translations.literal: " Sengshao said: "A man of mountains and marshes should properly bore through the wall to escape; if he cannot refuse the command, then he should follow the precedent of Duke Dai."
translations.idiomatic: " Sengshao said: "A man of the hills and wilds ought to break through the wall and flee; if I cannot refuse the summons, I shall follow the example of Dai Andao."

sentences.zh: 」永明元年，世祖敕召僧紹，稱疾不肯見。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Yongming the heir summoned Sengshao by imperial order; he pleaded illness and refused to appear.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of Yongming, Emperor Wu summoned Sengshao by edict; he pleaded illness and would not appear.

sentences.zh: 詔徵國子博士，不就，卒。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him as Erudite of the National University; he did not accept and died.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him as Erudite of the National University; he declined and died.

sentences.zh: 子元琳，字仲璋，亦傳家業。

translations.literal: His son Yuanlin, styled Zhongzhang, also transmitted the family learning.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanlin, courtesy name Zhongzhang, also carried on the family tradition of learning.

sentences.zh: 長兄 僧胤

translations.literal: Elder brother Sengyin
translations.idiomatic: Elder brother Sengyin

sentences.zh: 僧紹長兄僧胤，能玄言。

translations.literal: Sengshao's elder brother Sengyin was skilled in arcane discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Sengshao's elder brother Sengyin was accomplished in arcane learning.

sentences.zh: 宋世爲冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the Song dynasty he was Inspector of Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Song he served as Inspector of Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 弟僧暠，亦好學，宋孝武見之，迎頌其名，時人以爲榮。

translations.literal: His younger brother Senggao also loved learning; Emperor Xiaowu of Song saw him and welcomed him with praise of his name; men of the time regarded this as an honor.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Senggao also loved learning; when Emperor Xiaowu of Song met him, he received him with praise of his name—a distinction men of the time counted as glory.

sentences.zh: 泰始初，爲青州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taishi he was Inspector of Qing Province.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Taishi he became Inspector of Qing Province.

sentences.zh: 慶符，建元初，爲黃門。

translations.literal: Qingfu, at the beginning of Jianyuan, was Yellow Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Qingfu, at the beginning of Jianyuan, served as Yellow Gate Attendant.

sentences.zh: 子 惠照

translations.literal: Son Huizhao
translations.idiomatic: Son Huizhao

sentences.zh: 僧胤子惠照，元徽中，爲太祖平南主簿，從拒桂陽，累至驃騎中兵，與荀伯玉對領直。

translations.literal: Sengyin's son Huizhao, in the Yuanhui era, was Registrar on the Pacify-the-South staff of the founder, followed him in resisting Guiyang, rose through posts to Central Troops under the Rapid Cavalry General, and with Xun Boyu jointly commanded the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Sengyin's son Huizhao, during Yuanhui, served the founder as Registrar on the Pacify-the-South staff, followed him in resisting the Guiyang rebellion, rose to Central Troops under the Rapid Cavalry General, and with Xun Boyu jointly commanded the palace guard.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，爲巴州刺史，綏懷蠻蜑，上許爲益州，未遷，卒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was Governor of Ba Province, pacified and won over the Man and Dan tribes; the throne approved his transfer to Yi Province, but before he moved he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan he became Governor of Ba Province, where he pacified the tribal peoples; the throne approved his transfer to Yi Province, but he died before taking up the new post.

sentences.zh: 顧歡字景怡，吳郡鹽官人也。

translations.literal: Gu Huan, styled Jingyi, was a native of Yanguan in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Huan, courtesy name Jingyi, came from Yanguan in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖赳，晉隆安末，避亂徙居。

translations.literal: His grandfather Qiu, at the end of Long'an in Jin, moved to escape the turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qiu moved there at the end of the Long'an era to escape the turmoil.

sentences.zh: 歡年六七歲書甲子，有簡三篇，歡析計，遂知六甲。

translations.literal: When Huan was six or seven he wrote the sexagenary cycle; there were three bamboo slips, and Huan analyzed and calculated until he knew the six jia.
translations.idiomatic: At six or seven Huan wrote out the sexagenary cycle; given three bamboo slips to work from, he calculated his way through and mastered the full cycle.

sentences.zh: 家貧，父使驅田中雀，歡作《黃雀賦》而歸，雀食過半，父怒，欲撻之，見賦乃止。

translations.literal: The family was poor; his father sent him to drive sparrows from the fields. Huan composed an "Ode to the Yellow Sparrow" and returned; the sparrows had eaten more than half the crop. His father was angry and meant to beat him, but on seeing the ode he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor; his father sent him to chase sparrows from the fields. Huan came back having written an "Ode to the Yellow Sparrow," but the birds had already eaten more than half the crop. His father flew into a rage and was about to thrash him—until he read the ode and stayed his hand.

sentences.zh: 郷中有學舍，歡貧無以受業，於舍壁後倚聽，無遺忘者。

translations.literal: In the village was a school; Huan was too poor to receive instruction and listened leaning against the wall behind the schoolhouse, forgetting nothing.
translations.idiomatic: There was a village school, but Huan was too poor to enroll; he listened from behind the wall and forgot nothing he heard.

sentences.zh: 八歲，誦《孝經》、《詩》、《論》。

translations.literal: At eight he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Odes, and the Analects.
translations.idiomatic: By eight he could recite the Classic of Filial Piety, the Odes, and the Analects.

sentences.zh: 及長，篤志好學。

translations.literal: When grown, he was steadfast in purpose and loved learning.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew older, he pursued learning with steadfast devotion.

sentences.zh: 母年老，躬耕誦書，夜則燃糠自照。

translations.literal: His mother was old; he personally plowed and recited books, and at night burned chaff to light himself.
translations.idiomatic: His mother was elderly; he farmed by day while reciting his texts, and at night burned chaff for light to read by.

sentences.zh: 同郡顧顗之臨縣，見而異之，遣諸子與遊，及孫憲之，竝受經句。

translations.literal: Gu Yanzhi of the same commandery, on taking office as magistrate, saw him and marveled, sent his sons to associate with him, and Sun Xianzhi as well—all received his instruction in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Yanzhi of the same commandery came to serve as county magistrate, he was struck by Huan's gifts and sent his sons to study with him, as did Sun Xianzhi—all received instruction in the classics from him.

sentences.zh: 歡年二十餘，更從豫章雷次宗諮玄儒諸義。

translations.literal: When Huan was in his twenties he went further to Lei Cizong of Yuzhang to inquire into the various meanings of arcane and Confucian learning.
translations.idiomatic: In his twenties Huan went on to Lei Cizong of Yuzhang to pursue the arcane and Confucian teachings.

sentences.zh: 母亡，水漿不入口六七日，廬于墓次，遂隱遁不仕。

translations.literal: When his mother died he took no food or drink for six or seven days, built a hut by the grave, and thereafter withdrew and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother died he took no food or drink for six or seven days, built a mourning hut beside her grave, and thereafter lived in seclusion, refusing office.

sentences.zh: 於剡天台山開館聚徒，受業者常近百人。

translations.literal: On Mount Tiantai in Shan he opened a hall and gathered disciples; those receiving instruction often numbered nearly a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: On Mount Tiantai in Shan he opened a school and gathered students; his pupils often numbered nearly a hundred.

sentences.zh: 歡早孤，每讀《詩》至「哀哀父母」。

translations.literal: Huan was orphaned early; whenever he read the Odes to the line "Alas, alas, my parents,"
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned early, whenever Huan read the Odes and came to the line "Alas, alas, my parents,"

sentences.zh: 輙執書慟泣，學者由是廢《蓼莪篇》不復講。

translations.literal: he would clutch the book and weep in grief; therefore his students discontinued the "Laolao" chapter and no longer lectured on it.
translations.idiomatic: he would clutch the book and weep; his students therefore stopped teaching the "Laolao" ode altogether.

sentences.zh: 太祖輔政，悅歡風教，徵爲揚州主簿，遣中使迎歡。

translations.literal: When the founder assisted in government he admired Huan's moral influence, summoned him as Registrar of Yang Province, and sent a palace envoy to welcome Huan.
translations.idiomatic: While assisting at court, the founder admired Huan's moral influence, summoned him as Registrar of Yang Province, and sent a palace envoy to escort him.

sentences.zh: 及踐阼，乃至。

translations.literal: When he ascended the throne, Huan then came.
translations.idiomatic: When the founder took the throne, Huan at last came.

sentences.zh: 歡稱山谷臣顧歡上表曰：「臣聞舉網提綱，振裘持領，綱領旣理，毛目自張。

translations.literal: Huan styled himself Gu Huan, subject of the mountain valleys, and submitted a memorial saying: "Your subject has heard that to lift the net one takes the cord, to shake the fur coat one grasps the collar—once cord and collar are set right, the hairs and eyes spread of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Huan styled himself Gu Huan, subject of the mountain valleys, and submitted a memorial: "Your subject has heard that to lift a net one must take hold of the cord, and to shake out a fur coat one must grasp the collar—once the leading strands are set right, the lesser threads fall into place of themselves.

sentences.zh: 然則道德，綱也；

translations.literal: Thus virtue and the Way are the cord;
translations.idiomatic: Virtue and the Way are the cord;

sentences.zh: 物勢，目也。

translations.literal: the forms of things are the eyes.
translations.idiomatic: the forms of things are the mesh.

sentences.zh: 上理其綱，則萬機時序；

translations.literal: When the ruler sets the cord in order, the myriad affairs proceed in season;
translations.idiomatic: When the ruler orders the leading strand, the myriad affairs fall into season;

sentences.zh: 下張其目，則庶官不曠。

translations.literal: when those below spread the eyes, the host of officials are not idle.
translations.idiomatic: when those below spread the mesh, the host of officials are not remiss.

sentences.zh: 是以湯、武得勢師道則祚延，秦、項忽道任勢則身戮。

translations.literal: Therefore Tang and Wu, gaining power and taking the Way as teacher, extended their reigns; Qin and Xiang, neglecting the Way and relying on power, were put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Tang and Wu, gaining power while honoring the Way as teacher, prolonged their rule; Qin and Xiang, neglecting the Way while trusting in force alone, perished by the sword.

sentences.zh: 夫天門開闔，自古有之，四氣相新，絺裘代進。

translations.literal: The opening and closing of the Gate of Heaven have existed since antiquity; the four seasons renew one another, and thin silk and fur coats succeed each other.
translations.idiomatic: The opening and closing of heaven's gate have been so since antiquity; the four seasons renew one another, and light silk gives way to fur.

sentences.zh: 今火澤易位，三靈改憲，天樹明德，對時育物，搜揚仄陋，野無伏言。

translations.literal: Now Fire and Lake have exchanged positions, the three numina have changed their charter; Heaven has planted bright virtue, responding to the season and nurturing things, searching out and elevating the lowly and obscure, and in the wilds none keep silent counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Now Fire and Lake have changed places, the three numina have altered their mandate; Heaven has planted bright virtue in you, that you may respond to the age and nurture all things, seeking out the humble and obscure, so that no worthy voice in the wilds goes unheard.

sentences.zh: 是以窮谷愚夫，敢露偏管，謹刪撰《老氏》，獻《治綱》一卷。

translations.literal: Therefore this poor fool of a ravine dares to reveal his narrow pipe, respectfully abridging and composing the Laozi and presenting one fascicle of "Principles of Governance."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore this ignorant man of the deep valleys dares offer his humble counsel, having abridged the Laozi and respectfully presenting one fascicle entitled "Principles of Governance."

sentences.zh: 伏願稽古百王，斟酌時用，不以芻蕘棄言，不以人微廢道，則率土之賜也，微臣之幸也。

translations.literal: Your subject bows and hopes you will examine the hundred kings of antiquity and weigh what suits the present age, not discarding words because they are mere firewood counsel, not abandoning the Way because the man is insignificant—then it would be a gift to all within the seas and the good fortune of this humble subject.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly pray that you will examine the hundred kings of antiquity and weigh what suits the present age, neither discarding counsel because it comes from the grass roots nor abandoning the Way because the man is insignificant—this would be a blessing to all within the seas and the good fortune of your humble subject.

sentences.zh: 幸賜一疏，則上下交泰，雖不求民而民悅，不祈天而天應，應天悅民，則皇基固矣。

translations.literal: If you would grant one memorial, then above and below would interchange in peace; though you do not seek the people, the people would be pleased; though you do not pray to Heaven, Heaven would respond—responding to Heaven and pleasing the people, the imperial foundation would be secure.
translations.idiomatic: If you would grant this one memorial a hearing, above and below would be at peace; though you do not court the people, they would rejoice; though you do not pray to Heaven, Heaven would answer—when Heaven answers and the people rejoice, the imperial foundation stands firm.

sentences.zh: 臣志盡幽深，無與榮勢，自足雲霞，不須祿養。

translations.literal: Your subject's will is spent in the deep and remote; he has no share in glory and power, is self-sufficient among clouds and mist, and needs no salary to sustain him.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject's aspirations lie wholly in the deep wilds; I have no part in glory or power, am content among clouds and mist, and need no stipend to live.

sentences.zh: 陛下旣遠見尋求，敢不盡言。

translations.literal: Since Your Majesty has sought me from afar, how dare I not speak fully?
translations.idiomatic: Since Your Majesty has sought me out from afar, how could I not speak my mind fully?

sentences.zh: 言旣盡矣，請從此退。」

translations.literal: My words are now exhausted; I beg to withdraw from here."
translations.idiomatic: I have said all I have to say; I beg leave to withdraw."

sentences.zh: 是時員外郎劉思效表陳讜言曰：「宋自大明以來，漸見凋弊，徵賦有增於往，天府尤貧於昔。

translations.literal: At this time the Acting Palace Gentleman Liu Sixiao submitted a memorial of blunt counsel saying: "Since the Daming era of Song, decline has gradually appeared; levies have increased over the past, and the imperial treasury is especially poorer than before.
translations.idiomatic: At this time the Acting Palace Gentleman Liu Sixiao submitted a memorial of blunt counsel: "Since the Daming era of Song, decline has set in; levies have risen above what they once were, and the imperial treasury is poorer than ever.

sentences.zh: 兼軍警屢興，傷夷不復，戍役殘丁，儲無半菽，小民嗷嗷，無樂生之色。

translations.literal: Moreover military alarms have repeatedly arisen, wounds and losses are not restored, garrison labor wears out the remaining men, stores hold not half a bean, and the common people cry out with no look of joy in living.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover military alarms have recurred again and again; the wounded are not restored, garrison labor exhausts what men remain, the granaries hold scarcely a handful of grain, and the common people cry out with no joy left in living.

sentences.zh: 貴勢之流，貨室之族，車服伎樂，爭相奢麗，亭池第宅，競趣高華。

translations.literal: The streams of noble power and families of wealthy chambers vie in extravagant carriages, robes, performers, and music, and in pavilions, pools, and mansions rush to the lofty and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: The powerful and wealthy vie in extravagant carriages, robes, performers, and music, and compete to build the loftiest pavilions, pools, and mansions.

sentences.zh: 至於山澤之人，不敢採飲其水草。

translations.literal: As for people of mountains and marshes, they dare not gather and drink its grasses and waters.
translations.idiomatic: Even those who dwell in hills and marshes dare not gather herbs or drink from the streams.

sentences.zh: 貧富相輝，捐源尚末。

translations.literal: Rich and poor reflect each other in splendor; sources are squandered and the end is not yet reached.
translations.idiomatic: Rich and poor glare at one another across a widening gap; the springs of prosperity run dry, and the worst is not yet over.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜發明詔，吐德音，布惠澤，禁邪偽，薄賦斂，省傜役，絕奇麗之賂，塞鄭、衞之倡，變曆運之化，應質文之用，不亦大哉！

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought to issue a clear edict, give forth a voice of virtue, spread beneficent grace, prohibit wicked falsehood, lighten taxes and levies, reduce corvée labor, cut off extravagant and splendid bribes, block the licentious songs of Zheng and Wei, transform the change of dynastic fortune, and respond to the uses of substance and culture — would that not be great!
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should issue a clear edict, proclaim virtue, spread grace, forbid falsehood, lighten taxes, reduce corvée, end extravagant gifts, suppress the licentious music of Zheng and Wei, turn the tide of dynastic fortune, and meet the needs of an age that calls for substance over ornament — how great an achievement that would be!

sentences.zh: 又彭、汴有鴟梟之巢，青丘爲狐兔之窟，虐害踰紀，殘暴日滋。

translations.literal: Moreover at Peng and Bian there are nests of owls and kites; Qingqiu has become a den of foxes and rabbits; oppression exceeds a full cycle of years, and cruelty grows daily.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Peng and Bian have become nests of owls and kites, and Qingqiu a warren of foxes and rabbits; tyranny has lasted beyond a full cycle of years, and brutality grows worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 鬼泣舊泉，人悲故壤，童孺視編髮而慚生，耆老看左衽而恥沒。

translations.literal: Ghosts weep at old springs; people grieve their former soil; children seeing braided hair are ashamed to live; elders seeing left-lapel dress are shamed in death.
translations.idiomatic: Ghosts weep at the old springs; the people mourn their lost homeland; children who see braided barbarian hair are ashamed to go on living, and elders who see left-lapel dress are shamed even in death.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜仰答天人引領之望，下弔甿黎傾首之勤，授鉞衞、霍之將，遺策蕭、張之師，萬道俱前，窮山蕩谷。

translations.literal: Your Majesty ought above to answer heaven and men who stretch their necks in hope, below to console the common people who bow their heads in toil, confer battle-axes on generals like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, send forth strategists like Xiao He and Zhang Liang, advance on ten thousand roads, and sweep through mountains to the ends of valleys.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should answer above the hopes of heaven and men who stretch their necks in longing, and below console the common people who bow their heads in weary toil; appoint generals like Wei Qing and Huo Qubing, send forth strategists like Xiao He and Zhang Liang, advance on every road, and sweep from the farthest mountains to the deepest valleys.

sentences.zh: 此卽恒山不足指而傾，渤海不足飲而竭，豈徒殘寇塵滅而已哉！」

translations.literal: Then even Mount Heng would not suffice to point at for toppling, and the Bohai Sea would not suffice to drink and drain — would it be merely eliminating the remaining bandits and dust?"
translations.idiomatic: Then even Mount Heng would not be enough to point to as a measure of what would fall, nor the Bohai Sea enough to drink dry — and would the victory be merely the wiping out of scattered bandits and dust?"

sentences.zh: 上詔曰：「朕夙旦惟夤，思弘治道，佇夢巖濱，垂精管庫，旰食縈懷，其勤至矣。

translations.literal: The emperor issued an edict saying: "I rise early and stay late, thinking to expand the way of governance, awaiting the dream of Yan Bank, devoting my spirit to treasury and granary, eating after sunset with care ever bound to me — my diligence has reached its utmost.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued an edict: "I rise early and retire late, seeking to broaden the way of governance; I await the sage of Yan Bank in my dreams and devote my attention to treasury and granary; I eat after sunset, my mind never at rest — my diligence could hardly be greater.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧歡、散騎郎劉思效，或至自丘園，或越在冗位，竝能獻書金門，薦辭鳳闕，辨章治體，有協朕心。

translations.literal: Gu Huan of Wu commandery and Palace Attendant Liu Sixiao — one came from garden and field, one was promoted from a redundant post — both were able to submit writings at the Golden Gate, present words at the Phoenix Tower, distinguish and set forth the substance of governance, and accord with my heart.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Huan of Wu commandery and Palace Attendant Liu Sixiao — one came from seclusion in field and garden, one was raised from a superfluous post — both submitted memorials at the Golden Gate and presented counsel at the Phoenix Tower, clarifying the principles of governance in ways that accord with my intent.

sentences.zh: 今出其表，外可詳擇所宜，以時敷奏。

translations.literal: Now publish their memorials; the outer court may carefully select what is suitable and present reports in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Let their memorials be published; the outer court should carefully choose what is fitting and report on it in due course.

sentences.zh: 歡近已加旍賁，思效可付選銓序，以顯讜言。

translations.literal: Huan has recently been given banner and honors; Sixiao may be entrusted to the selection and ranking offices to display blunt counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Huan has recently been honored with banner and reward; Sixiao may be assigned to the offices of selection and ranking, that his blunt counsel may be made visible.

sentences.zh: 」歡東歸，上賜麈尾、素琴。

translations.literal: " Huan returned east; the emperor bestowed on him a fly-whisk and a plain zither.
translations.idiomatic: " Huan returned east, and the emperor gave him a deer-tail fly-whisk and a plain zither.

sentences.zh: 永明元年，詔徵歡爲太學博士，同郡顧黯爲散騎郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongming, an edict summoned Huan as Docent of the Grand Academy, and Gu An of the same commandery as Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Yongming, an edict summoned Huan to serve as Docent of the Grand Academy and Gu An of the same commandery as Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 黯字長孺，有隱操，與歡俱不就徵。

translations.literal: An was styled Changru, possessed a hermit's character, and with Huan both declined the summons.
translations.idiomatic: An, styled Changru, had the character of a recluse; he and Huan both declined the summons.

sentences.zh: 歡晚節服食，不與人通。

translations.literal: In his later years Huan took elixirs and did not associate with people.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Huan took immortality elixirs and kept apart from others.

sentences.zh: 每旦出戶，山鳥集其掌取食。

translations.literal: Each morning when he went out his door, mountain birds gathered on his palm to take food.
translations.idiomatic: Each morning when he stepped outside, mountain birds would gather on his palm to be fed.

sentences.zh: 事黃老道，解陰陽書，爲數術多效驗。

translations.literal: He practiced the Way of Huang-Lao, understood books of yin and yang, and in numerological arts many things were verified effective.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Way of Huang-Lao, mastered the texts of yin and yang, and in numerological arts many of his methods proved effective.

sentences.zh: 初元嘉末，出都寄住東府，忽題柱云：「三十年二月二十一日。

translations.literal: Initially at the end of Yuanjia, when leaving the capital he lodged at the Eastern Mansion and suddenly wrote on a pillar, saying: "The thirtieth year, second month, twenty-first day.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, at the end of the Yuanjia era, when he was leaving the capital and lodging at the Eastern Mansion, he suddenly wrote on a pillar: "The thirtieth year, second month, twenty-first day.

sentences.zh: 」因東歸。

translations.literal: " Then he returned east.
translations.idiomatic: " Then he returned east.

sentences.zh: 後太初弒逆，果是此年月。

translations.literal: Later, in the Taichu regicide and rebellion, it was indeed this year and month.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when the Taichu regicide and rebellion occurred, it was indeed that year and month.

sentences.zh: 自知將終，賦詩言志云：「精氣因天行，遊魂隨物化。

translations.literal: Knowing that his end was near, he composed a poem expressing his intent, saying: "Essence and qi follow heaven's motion; the wandering soul follows things in transformation.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing that his end was near, he composed a poem to express his intent: "Essence and breath move with heaven; the wandering soul follows things into change.

sentences.zh: 」剋死日，卒於剡山，身體柔軟，時年六十四。

translations.literal: " On the day he had fixed for his death, he died on Mount Shan; his body remained soft, and he was sixty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: " On the day he had foretold for his death, he died on Mount Shan; his body remained supple. He was sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 還葬舊墓，木連理出墓側，縣令江山圖表狀。

translations.literal: He was returned and buried at his old tomb; trees with joined trunks grew beside the grave, and the magistrate Jiang Shan submitted a report with a diagram.
translations.idiomatic: He was buried in his old tomb; trees with conjoined trunks sprang up beside the grave, and Magistrate Jiang Shan submitted a report illustrated with a diagram.

sentences.zh: 世祖詔歡諸子，撰歡《文議》三十卷。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu ordered Huan's sons to compile Huan's Literary Discourses in thirty volumes.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu ordered Huan's sons to compile Huan's Literary Discourses in thirty volumes.

sentences.zh: 佛道二家，立教旣異，學者互相非毀。

translations.literal: The two schools of Buddhism and Daoism, in establishing their teachings, were already different, and scholars mutually slandered and attacked one another.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism and Daoism, in the teachings they established, already differed, and their followers slandered and attacked one another.

sentences.zh: 歡著《夷夏論》曰：

translations.literal: Huan wrote On Barbarians and Chinese, saying:
translations.idiomatic: Huan wrote On Barbarians and Chinese, which reads:

sentences.zh: 夫辨是與非，宜據聖典。

translations.literal: In distinguishing right from wrong, one ought to rely on the sacred classics.
translations.idiomatic: In distinguishing right from wrong, one should rely on the sacred classics.

sentences.zh: 尋二教之源，故兩標經句。

translations.literal: Tracing the sources of the two teachings, I therefore mark passages from both scriptures.
translations.idiomatic: Tracing the origins of the two teachings, I therefore cite passages from both scriptures.

sentences.zh: 道經云：「老子入關之天竺維衞國，國王夫人名曰淨妙，老子因其晝寢，乘日精入淨妙口中，後年四月八日夜半時，剖左腋而生，墜地卽行七步，於是佛道興焉。

translations.literal: The Daoist scripture says: "Laozi, upon passing the frontier gate, went to the land of Vaiśālī in India; the king's consort was named Pure Excellence. Laozi, because she was sleeping by day, rode the sun's essence into Pure Excellence's mouth. In the following year, at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month, he was born by cutting open her left side; upon falling to earth he immediately walked seven steps — and thus Buddhism arose.
translations.idiomatic: The Daoist scripture says: "When Laozi passed through the frontier gate and went to Vaiśālī in India, the king's consort was named Pure Excellence. While she slept by day, Laozi entered her mouth riding the sun's essence. The next year, at midnight on the eighth day of the fourth month, he was born by cutting open her left side; the moment he touched the ground he walked seven steps — and thus Buddhism arose.

sentences.zh: 」此出《玄妙內篇》。

translations.literal: " This comes from the Mysterious Marvels Inner Chapters.
translations.idiomatic: " This is from the Mysterious Marvels Inner Chapters.

sentences.zh: 佛經云：「釋迦成佛，有塵劫之數。

translations.literal: The Buddhist scripture says: "When Śākyamuni became a buddha, there were countless aeons in number.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist scripture says: "When Śākyamuni attained buddhahood, the number of aeons was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 」出《法華無量壽》。

translations.literal: " This comes from the Lotus Sutra of Immeasurable Life.
translations.idiomatic: " This is from the Lotus Sutra of Immeasurable Life.

sentences.zh: 或「爲國師道士，儒林之宗」。

translations.literal: Or: "as National Master and Daoist priest, leader of the Confucian forest."
translations.idiomatic: Or: "as National Master and Daoist priest, leader of the Confucian forest."

sentences.zh: 出《瑞應本起》。

translations.literal: This comes from the Auspicious Responses at the Original Rise.
translations.idiomatic: This is from the Auspicious Responses at the Original Rise.

sentences.zh: 歡論之曰：五帝、三皇，莫不有師。

translations.literal: Huan argued, saying: "The Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns all had teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Huan argued: "The Five Emperors and Three Sovereigns all had teachers.

sentences.zh: 國師道士，無過老、莊，儒林之宗，孰出周、孔。

translations.literal: As National Master and Daoist priest, none surpass Laozi and Zhuangzi; as leader of the Confucian forest, who exceeds the Duke of Zhou and Confucius?
translations.idiomatic: As National Master and Daoist priest, none surpass Laozi and Zhuangzi; as leader of the Confucian forest, who exceeds the Duke of Zhou and Confucius?

sentences.zh: 若孔、老非佛，誰則當之。

translations.literal: If Confucius and Laozi are not the Buddha, who then qualifies?
translations.idiomatic: If Confucius and Laozi are not the Buddha, who else could qualify?

sentences.zh: 然二經所說，如合符契。

translations.literal: Yet what the two scriptures say matches like fitting tally strips.
translations.idiomatic: Yet what the two scriptures say fits together like matching halves of a tally.

sentences.zh: 道則佛也，佛則道也。

translations.literal: The Way is the Buddha; the Buddha is the Way.
translations.idiomatic: The Way is the Buddha; the Buddha is the Way.

sentences.zh: 其聖則符，其迹則反。

translations.literal: In sainthood they match; in traces they reverse.
translations.idiomatic: In sainthood they accord; in outward traces they diverge.

sentences.zh: 或和光以明近；

translations.literal: One harmonizes light to illumine what is near;
translations.idiomatic: One harmonizes its light to illumine what is near;

sentences.zh: 或曜靈以示遠。

translations.literal: one displays spirit to show what is far.
translations.idiomatic: the other displays its radiance to reveal what is far.

sentences.zh: 道濟天下，故無方而不入；

translations.literal: The Way saves all under heaven, so there is no direction into which it does not enter;
translations.idiomatic: The Way saves all under heaven, and so enters every quarter;

sentences.zh: 智周萬物，故無物而不爲。

translations.literal: wisdom encompasses the myriad things, so there is nothing it does not do.
translations.idiomatic: wisdom encompasses the myriad things, and so there is nothing it will not do.

sentences.zh: 其入不同，其爲必異。

translations.literal: Their entry differs, so their doing must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Because their entry differs, what they do must differ as well.

sentences.zh: 各成其性，不易其事。

translations.literal: Each completes its nature and does not change its affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Each fulfills its own nature and does not alter its proper work.

sentences.zh: 是以端委搢紳，諸華之容；

translations.literal: Therefore formal robes and belted sashes are the appearance of the civilized peoples;
translations.idiomatic: Hence formal robes and belted sashes are the bearing of the civilized peoples;

sentences.zh: 翦髮曠衣，羣夷之服。

translations.literal: cropped hair and open robes are the garb of the barbarian multitudes.
translations.idiomatic: cropped hair and open robes are the dress of the barbarian peoples.

sentences.zh: 擎跽磬折，侯甸之恭；

translations.literal: holding up the knees and bending like a bell clapper are the courtesy of marquis and field domains;
translations.idiomatic: Holding up the knees and bowing low are the courtesies of lords and vassals;

sentences.zh: 狐蹲狗踞，荒流之肅。

translations.literal: squatting like foxes and crouching like dogs are the solemnity of the wild frontier.
translations.idiomatic: squatting like foxes and crouching like dogs are the solemnities of the wild frontier.

sentences.zh: 棺殯槨葬，中夏之制；

translations.literal: coffin, bier, outer coffin, and burial are the institutions of the Middle Kingdom;
translations.idiomatic: Coffin, bier, outer coffin, and burial are the customs of the Middle Kingdom;

sentences.zh: 火焚水沈，西戎之俗。

translations.literal: burning by fire and sinking in water are the customs of the Western Rong.
translations.idiomatic: cremation and water burial are the customs of the Western barbarians.

sentences.zh: 全形守禮，繼善之教；

translations.literal: preserving the body and keeping to ritual is the teaching of continuing goodness;
translations.idiomatic: Preserving the body and keeping to ritual is the teaching that continues goodness;

sentences.zh: 毀貌易性，絕惡之學。

translations.literal: destroying appearance and changing nature is the learning of cutting off evil.
translations.idiomatic: destroying one's appearance and altering one's nature is the learning that cuts off evil.

sentences.zh: 豈伊同人，爰及異物。

translations.literal: How could it be the same person, extending even to different creatures?
translations.idiomatic: How could these be the same teaching, extending even to different kinds of beings?

sentences.zh: 鳥王獸長，往往是佛，無窮世界，聖人代興。

translations.literal: Bird kings and beast chiefs are often the Buddha; in infinite worlds sages rise in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Kings among birds and chiefs among beasts are often buddhas; in endless worlds sages arise in succession.

sentences.zh: 或昭五典，或布三乘。

translations.literal: Some proclaim the Five Classics; some spread the Three Vehicles.
translations.idiomatic: Some proclaim the Five Classics; others spread the Three Vehicles.

sentences.zh: 在鳥而鳥鳴，在獸而獸吼。

translations.literal: Among birds they bird-call; among beasts they beast-roar.
translations.idiomatic: Among birds they speak as birds; among beasts they roar as beasts.

sentences.zh: 教華而華言，化夷而夷語耳。

translations.literal: Teaching the civilized in civilized speech, transforming barbarians in barbarian language — that is all.
translations.idiomatic: They teach the civilized in civilized speech and transform barbarians in barbarian tongues — that is all.

sentences.zh: 雖舟車均於致遠，而有川陸之節，佛道齊乎達化，而有夷夏之別，若謂其致旣均，其法可換者，而車可涉川，舟可行陸乎？

translations.literal: Although boats and carriages alike serve to reach far distances, there are distinctions between river and land; although Buddhism and the Way alike achieve transformation, there is a difference between barbarian and Chinese — if one says their ends are already equal and their methods may be exchanged, can a carriage cross a river, or a boat travel on land?
translations.idiomatic: Boats and carriages alike serve to reach far destinations, yet each has its place on water or land; Buddhism and the Way alike lead to transformation, yet there is a distinction between barbarian and Chinese. If one says their ends are already the same and their methods interchangeable, can a carriage cross a river, or a boat travel on land?

sentences.zh: 今以中夏之性，效西戎之法，旣不全同，又不全異。

translations.literal: Now, using the nature of the Middle Kingdom to imitate the methods of the Western Rong, one is neither wholly the same nor wholly different.
translations.idiomatic: Now, when people of the Middle Kingdom imitate the ways of the Western barbarians, the result is neither wholly the same nor wholly different.

sentences.zh: 下棄妻孥，上廢宗祀。

translations.literal: Below one abandons wife and children; above one abolishes ancestral sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Below, one abandons wife and children; above, one forsakes ancestral sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 嗜欲之物，皆以禮伸；

translations.literal: Objects of desire are all extended by ritual;
translations.idiomatic: Objects of desire are all given their proper place by ritual;

sentences.zh: 孝敬之典，獨以法屈。

translations.literal: the canon of filial respect alone is bent by religious law.
translations.idiomatic: yet the canon of filial respect alone is bent by religious law.

sentences.zh: 悖禮犯順，曾莫之覺。

translations.literal: Violating ritual and transgressing proper order — none ever notices.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual is violated and proper order transgressed, yet no one seems to notice.

sentences.zh: 弱喪忘歸，孰識其舊？

translations.literal: Lost in youth, forgetting return — who recognizes what was old?
translations.idiomatic: Lost since childhood, they forget the way home — who still recognizes the old ways?

sentences.zh: 且理之可貴者，道也；

translations.literal: Moreover, what is valuable in principle is the Way;
translations.idiomatic: What is valuable in principle is the Way;

sentences.zh: 事之可賤者，俗也。

translations.literal: what is base in affairs is custom.
translations.idiomatic: what is base in practice is custom.

sentences.zh: 捨華效夷，義將安取？

translations.literal: Abandoning civilization to imitate barbarians — where is the principle to be found?
translations.idiomatic: To abandon civilization and imitate barbarians — where is the principle in that?

sentences.zh: 若以道邪？

translations.literal: If for the sake of the Way?
translations.idiomatic: If it is for the sake of the Way?

sentences.zh: 道固符合矣。

translations.literal: The Way indeed accords.
translations.idiomatic: The Way itself already accords.

sentences.zh: 若以俗邪？

translations.literal: If for the sake of custom?
translations.idiomatic: If it is for the sake of custom?

sentences.zh: 俗則大乖矣。

translations.literal: Custom then greatly deviates.
translations.idiomatic: Custom then deviates greatly.

sentences.zh: 屢見刻舷沙門，守株道士，交諍小大，互相彈射。

translations.literal: One repeatedly sees mark-the-boat monks and tree-stump-guarding Daoists, disputing great and small matters and mutually attacking one another.
translations.idiomatic: Again and again one sees monks who mark the boat and Daoists who guard the tree stump, disputing matters great and small and attacking one another.

sentences.zh: 或域道以爲兩，或混俗以爲一。

translations.literal: Some fence the Way into two; some mix customs into one.
translations.idiomatic: Some fence the Way off into two separate teachings; others mix customs together as if they were one.

sentences.zh: 是牽異以爲同，破同以爲異。

translations.literal: That is dragging difference to make sameness, and breaking sameness to make difference.
translations.idiomatic: That is to drag difference into sameness and break sameness into difference.

sentences.zh: 則乖爭之由，淆亂之本也。

translations.literal: Then this is the cause of perverse contention and the root of confusion.
translations.idiomatic: This is the source of perverse contention and the root of confusion.

sentences.zh: 尋聖道雖同，而法有左右。

translations.literal: Tracing it: the sacred Way is the same, yet the methods have left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred Way is one, yet the methods differ in emphasis.

sentences.zh: 始乎無端，終乎無末。

translations.literal: It begins without origin and ends without termination.
translations.idiomatic: It begins without origin and ends without end.

sentences.zh: 泥洹仙化，各是一術。

translations.literal: Nirvana and immortal transformation — each is one technique.
translations.idiomatic: Nirvana and immortal transformation are each a distinct technique.

sentences.zh: 佛號正真，道稱正一。

translations.literal: The Buddha is titled Correct Truth; the Way is called Correct One.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha is called Correct Truth; the Way is called Correct One.

sentences.zh: 一歸無死，真會無生。

translations.literal: One returns to no death; true meeting is without birth.
translations.idiomatic: One returns to deathlessness; true union is birthlessness.

sentences.zh: 在名則反，在實則合。

translations.literal: In name they reverse; in substance they unite.
translations.idiomatic: In name they diverge; in substance they unite.

sentences.zh: 但無生之教賒，無死之化切。

translations.literal: But the teaching of no-birth is distant, while the transformation of no-death is urgent.
translations.idiomatic: But the teaching of no-birth is deferred, while the transformation of no-death is immediate.

sentences.zh: 切法可以進謙弱，賒法可以退夸強。

translations.literal: The urgent method can advance humility and weakness; the distant method can retreat from arrogance and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The immediate method can advance humility in the weak; the deferred method can restrain arrogance in the strong.

sentences.zh: 佛教文而博，道教質而精。

translations.literal: Buddhism is cultured and broad; Daoism is plain and refined.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is literary and broad; Daoism is plain and refined.

sentences.zh: 精非麤人所信，博非精人所能。

translations.literal: Refinement is not what coarse people believe; breadth is not what refined people can attain.
translations.idiomatic: Refinement is not for coarse minds to accept; breadth is not for refined minds to need.

sentences.zh: 佛言華而引，道言實而抑。

translations.literal: The Buddha's words are flowery and draw people in; the Way's words are solid and restrain them.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha's words are ornate and draw people forward; the Way's words are plain and hold people back.

sentences.zh: 抑則明者獨進，引則昧者競前。

translations.literal: Restraining, the clear advance alone; drawing, the obscure vie to press forward.
translations.idiomatic: Restraint lets the clear-minded advance alone; allurement makes the dull-minded rush forward in competition.

sentences.zh: 佛經繁而顯，道經簡而幽。

translations.literal: Buddhist scriptures are complex and manifest; Daoist scriptures are simple and hidden.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhist scriptures are elaborate and explicit; Daoist scriptures are simple and obscure.

sentences.zh: 幽則妙門難見，顯則正路易遵。

translations.literal: Hidden, the subtle gate is hard to see; manifest, the correct path is easy to follow.
translations.idiomatic: What is obscure makes the subtle gate hard to see; what is explicit makes the correct path easy to follow.

sentences.zh: 此二法之辨也。

translations.literal: This is the distinction of the two methods.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the distinction between the two methods.

sentences.zh: 聖匠無心，方圓有體，器旣殊用，教亦異施。

translations.literal: The sacred craftsman is without fixed intent; square and round have their forms; vessels already differ in use, and teachings also differ in application.
translations.idiomatic: The sacred craftsman has no fixed intent; square and round each have their form. Vessels differ in use, and teachings differ in how they are applied.

sentences.zh: 佛是破惡之方，道是興善之術。

translations.literal: The Buddha is the method of breaking evil; the Way is the technique of promoting good.
translations.idiomatic: Buddhism is the method for breaking evil; the Way is the technique for promoting good.

sentences.zh: 興善則自然爲高，破惡則勇猛爲貴。

translations.literal: Promoting good, then naturalness is lofty; breaking evil, then courage is prized.
translations.idiomatic: In promoting good, naturalness is supreme; in breaking evil, courage is prized.

sentences.zh: 佛跡光大，宜以化物；

translations.literal: The Buddha's traces are vast and bright, suited to transforming creatures;
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha's traces are vast and luminous, suited to transforming others;

sentences.zh: 道跡密微，利用爲己。

translations.literal: the Way's traces are secret and subtle, useful for benefiting oneself.
translations.idiomatic: the Way's traces are subtle and hidden, useful for benefiting oneself.

sentences.zh: 優劣之分，大略在茲。

translations.literal: The division of superior and inferior lies broadly here.
translations.idiomatic: The broad distinction between superior and inferior lies here.

sentences.zh: 夫蹲夷之儀，婁羅之辯，各出彼俗，自相聆解。

translations.literal: As for squatting barbarian rites and Louluo debates, each arises from that custom and is mutually understood among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Squatting barbarian rites and Louluo-style disputation each arise from those customs and are understood only among themselves.

sentences.zh: 猶蟲嚾鳥聒，何足述效。

translations.literal: They are like insects chirping and birds clamoring — how worth describing and imitating?
translations.idiomatic: They are like the chirping of insects and the clamor of birds — what point is there in recounting or imitating them?

sentences.zh: 歡雖同二法，而意黨道教。

translations.literal: Although Huan harmonizes the two methods, in intent he favors the Way teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Although Gu Huan reconciles the two teachings, at heart he favors Daoism.

sentences.zh: 宋司徒袁粲託爲道人通公駮之，其略曰：

translations.literal: Song Grand Steward Yuan Can entrusted Daoist Master Tong Gong to refute it; the summary says:
translations.idiomatic: Song Grand Steward Yuan Can had the Daoist master Tong Gong refute him; the gist of his argument was:

sentences.zh: 白日停光，恒星隱照，誕降之應，事在老先，似非入關，方炳斯瑞。

translations.literal: The white sun halted its light, the fixed stars hid their illumination; responses to birth and descent — the matter was with Laozi first; it seems not at entering the pass that this auspicious sign appeared.
translations.idiomatic: When the sun stopped in the sky and the stars hid their light, these were signs of a sage's birth — and such signs attended Laozi first; they did not wait until he entered the pass to manifest.

sentences.zh: 又老、莊、周、孔，有可存者，依日末光，憑釋遺法，盜牛竊善，反以成蠹，檢究源流，終異吾黨之爲道耳。

translations.literal: Moreover, among Laozi, Zhuangzi, Zhou, and Confucius, what can be preserved relies on the sun's last light and leans on the Buddha's remaining law — stealing the ox and pilfering goodness until it becomes a pestilence; examining source and stream, in the end it differs from our faction's practice of the Way.
translations.idiomatic: As for Laozi, Zhuangzi, Zhou, and Confucius, what can be salvaged from their teachings leans on the waning light of the sun and borrows from Buddhist survivals — stealing the ox and pilfering goodness until it becomes a pestilence. Trace the source and stream, and in the end their Way is not the Way of our school.

sentences.zh: 西域之記，佛經之說，俗以膝行爲禮，不慕蹲坐爲恭，道以三繞爲虔，不尚踞傲爲肅。

translations.literal: Records of the Western Regions and Buddhist scriptures say that custom takes advancing on the knees as ritual and does not esteem squatting as respect; the Way takes three circumambulations as piety and does not value arrogant sprawling as solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: In Western Region records and Buddhist scriptures, custom treats advancing on the knees as ritual and does not esteem squatting as respect; the Way treats three circumambulations as piety and does not value arrogant sprawling as solemnity.

sentences.zh: 豈專戎土，爰亦茲方。

translations.literal: How could it be exclusive to Rong territory — it exists also in this region.
translations.idiomatic: Surely these are not exclusive to barbarian lands; they exist in our own realm as well.

sentences.zh: 襄童謁帝，膝行而進；

translations.literal: Xiang Tong, attending the emperor, advanced on his knees;
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Tong, attending upon the emperor, advanced on his knees;

sentences.zh: 趙王見周，三環而止。

translations.literal: the Lord of Zhao, meeting the Duke of Zhou, circled three times and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when the Lord of Zhao met the Duke of Zhou, he circled three times and stopped.

sentences.zh: 今佛法在華，乘者常安；

translations.literal: Now that Buddhist dharma is in China, those who ride it are always at peace;
translations.idiomatic: Now that the Buddhist dharma is in China, those who embrace it are always secure;

sentences.zh: 戒善行交，蹈者恒通。

translations.literal: precepts and good conduct intertwined, those who tread it are always unimpeded.
translations.idiomatic: precepts and good conduct intertwined, those who walk its path are always unimpeded.

sentences.zh: 文王造周，大伯創吳，革化戎夷，不因舊俗。

translations.literal: King Wen established Zhou, Taibo founded Wu — transforming and civilizing the Rong and Yi, not following old customs.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen established Zhou, and Taibo founded Wu — they transformed and civilized the barbarians without clinging to old customs.

sentences.zh: 豈若舟車，理無代用。

translations.literal: Are they not like boats and carriages — by principle there is no mutual substitution?
translations.idiomatic: Are they not like boats and carriages — by their nature they cannot substitute for one another?

sentences.zh: 佛法垂化，或因或革。

translations.literal: When Buddhist dharma spreads transformation, sometimes it follows and sometimes it reforms.
translations.idiomatic: When the Buddhist teaching spreads its transforming influence, sometimes it follows local custom and sometimes it reforms it.

sentences.zh: 清信之士，容衣不改；

translations.literal: Pure believers need not change appearance or dress;
translations.idiomatic: For pure believers, appearance and dress need not change;

sentences.zh: 息心之人，服貌必變。

translations.literal: those who still the mind must change dress and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: but those who still the mind must change dress and appearance.

sentences.zh: 變本從道，不遵彼俗，教風自殊，無患其亂。

translations.literal: Changing the root to follow the Way and not following those customs — teaching winds naturally differ, so there is no worry about disorder.
translations.idiomatic: To change one's root and follow the Way rather than those customs is to let teaching winds differ naturally — there is no need to fear disorder.

sentences.zh: 孔、老、釋迦，其人或同，觀方設教，其道必異。

translations.literal: Confucius, Laozi, and Shakyamuni — their persons may be the same, but observing each region they set forth teaching, and their paths must differ.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius, Laozi, and Shakyamuni — though their persons may be one, each observed his region and set forth teaching accordingly, and their paths must differ.

sentences.zh: 孔、老治世爲本，釋氏出世爲宗。

translations.literal: Confucius and Laozi take governing the world as foundation; the Shakya clan takes withdrawal from the world as core.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius and Laozi take governing the world as their foundation; the Shakya teaching takes withdrawal from the world as its core.

sentences.zh: 發軫旣殊，其歸亦異。

translations.literal: Since starting points already differ, their destinations also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Since their starting points already differ, their destinations differ as well.

sentences.zh: 符合之唱，自由臆說。

translations.literal: The claim that they accord is freely an imaginative assertion.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that they accord is nothing but a freely invented assertion.

sentences.zh: 又仙化以變形爲上，泥洹以陶神爲先。

translations.literal: Moreover, immortal transformation values changing form as supreme; nirvana values refining the spirit first.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, immortal transformation prizes changing the body as supreme, while nirvana prizes refining the spirit first.

sentences.zh: 變形者白首還緇，而未能無死；

translations.literal: Changing form means white hair returning to black, yet one still cannot escape death;
translations.idiomatic: Changing form means white hair turning black again, yet one still cannot escape death;

sentences.zh: 陶神者使塵惑日損，湛然常存。

translations.literal: refining the spirit means day by day reducing worldly defilements, tranquil and ever abiding.
translations.idiomatic: refining the spirit means day by day reducing worldly defilements until one is tranquil and ever abiding.

sentences.zh: 泥洹之道，無死之地，乖詭若此，何謂其同？

translations.literal: The Way of nirvana is a realm without death — so divergent as this; how can one call them the same?
translations.idiomatic: The Way of nirvana is a realm without death — so divergent as this; how can one call them the same?

sentences.zh: 歡答曰：

translations.literal: Huan replied:
translations.idiomatic: Gu Huan replied:

sentences.zh: 案道經之作，著自西周，佛經之來，始乎東漢，年踰八百，代懸數十。

translations.literal: Examining the composition of Daoist scriptures, they were written from the Western Zhou; Buddhist scriptures arrived only in the Eastern Han — more than eight hundred years apart, spanning dozens of dynastic generations.
translations.idiomatic: Examining the matter: Daoist scriptures were composed as early as the Western Zhou, while Buddhist scriptures arrived only in the Eastern Han — more than eight hundred years apart and spanning dozens of dynastic generations.

sentences.zh: 若謂黃老雖久，而濫在釋前，是呂尚盜陳恒之齊，劉季竊王莽之漢也。

translations.literal: If one says that although Huang-Lao is ancient, it was wrongly placed before the Buddha, that is like Lü Shang stealing Chen Heng's Qi, or Liu Ji stealing Wang Mang's Han.
translations.idiomatic: If one says that although Huang-Lao is ancient, it was wrongly placed before Buddhism, that is like saying Lü Shang stole Chen Heng's Qi, or Liu Ji stole Wang Mang's Han.

sentences.zh: 經云，戎氣強獷，乃復略人頰車邪？

translations.literal: Scripture says barbarian nature is fierce and untamed — would it then again seize upon people's cheek and jaw?
translations.idiomatic: Scripture says barbarian nature is fierce and untamed — would it then again seize upon people's cheek and jaw?

sentences.zh: 又夷俗長跽，法與華異，翹左跂右，全是蹲踞。

translations.literal: Moreover, barbarian custom favors long kneeling; its rites differ from China's — left foot raised, right foot on tiptoe, entirely squatting and crouching.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, barbarian custom favors long kneeling; its rites differ from China's — left foot raised, right foot on tiptoe, entirely a matter of squatting and crouching.

sentences.zh: 故周公禁之於前，仲尼戒之於後。

translations.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou forbade it earlier, and Confucius warned against it later.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the Duke of Zhou forbade it in earlier times, and Confucius warned against it afterward.

sentences.zh: 又舟以濟川，車以征陸，佛起於戎，豈非戎俗素惡邪？

translations.literal: Moreover, boats cross rivers and carriages travel on land; the Buddha arose among the Rong — is this not because Rong custom is inherently evil?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, boats cross rivers and carriages travel on land; the Buddha arose among the Rong — is this not because Rong customs are inherently evil?

sentences.zh: 道出於華，豈非華風本善邪？

translations.literal: The Way arose from China — is this not because Chinese custom is inherently good?
translations.idiomatic: The Way arose from China — is this not because Chinese custom is inherently good?

sentences.zh: 今華風旣變，惡同戎狄，佛來破之，良有以矣。

translations.literal: Now Chinese custom has already changed, becoming as evil as the Rong and Di; the Buddha came to break it — and with good reason.
translations.idiomatic: Now Chinese custom has already changed, becoming as evil as the Rong and Di; the Buddha came to break it — and with good reason.

sentences.zh: 佛道實貴，故戒業可遵；

translations.literal: The Buddhist Way is truly precious, so precepts and karma can be followed;
translations.idiomatic: The Buddhist Way is truly precious, so its precepts and karmic discipline can be followed;

sentences.zh: 戎俗實賤，故言貌可棄。

translations.literal: barbarian custom is truly base, so speech and appearance can be discarded.
translations.idiomatic: barbarian custom is truly base, so its speech and appearance can be discarded.

sentences.zh: 今諸華士女，民族弗革，而露首偏踞，濫用夷禮，云於翦落之徒，全是胡人，國有舊風，法不可變。

translations.literal: Now all Chinese men and women, their ethnicity unchanged, yet bare their heads and sit askew, abusing barbarian rites — saying of the tonsured that they are wholly barbarians; the state has old customs, and law cannot be changed.
translations.idiomatic: Now all Chinese men and women, their ethnicity unchanged, yet bare their heads and sit askew, abusing barbarian rites — saying of the tonsured that they are wholly barbarians; the state has its old customs, and law cannot be changed.

sentences.zh: 又若觀風流教，其道必異，佛非東華之道，道非西戎之法，魚鳥異淵，永不相關，安得老、釋二教，交行八表。

translations.literal: Moreover, if one observes customs to set forth teaching, the paths must differ; the Buddha is not the Way of Eastern China, and the Way is not the law of the Western Rong — fish and birds dwell in different depths and are forever unrelated; how can the two teachings of Laozi and the Buddha intercourse across the eight directions?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, if one observes customs to set forth teaching, the paths must differ; the Buddha is not the Way of Eastern China, and the Way is not the law of the Western Rong — fish and birds dwell in different depths and are forever unrelated; how can the two teachings of Laozi and the Buddha intercourse across the eight directions?

sentences.zh: 今佛旣東流，道亦西邁，故知世有精麤，教有文質。

translations.literal: Now the Buddha has already flowed east, and the Way has also advanced west — thus one knows the world has refined and coarse, and teachings have cultured and plain.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Buddha has already flowed east, and the Way has also advanced west — thus one knows the world has refined and coarse aspects, and teachings have cultured and plain forms.

sentences.zh: 然則道教執本以領末，佛教救末以存本。

translations.literal: Then Daoism grasps the root to lead the branches, while Buddhism saves the branches to preserve the root.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Daoism grasps the root to govern the branches, while Buddhism saves the branches to preserve the root.

sentences.zh: 請問所異，歸在何許？

translations.literal: May I ask where the difference lies — where does the return lie?
translations.idiomatic: Tell me, then: where does the difference lie — where does the return lie?

sentences.zh: 若以翦落爲異，則胥靡翦落矣。

translations.literal: If one takes tonsure as the difference, then criminals are tonsured too.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes tonsure as the difference, then criminals are tonsured too.

sentences.zh: 若以立像爲異，則俗巫立像矣。

translations.literal: If one takes erecting images as the difference, then folk shamans erect images too.
translations.idiomatic: If one takes erecting images as the difference, then folk shamans erect images too.

sentences.zh: 此非所歸，歸在常住。

translations.literal: These are not the return — the return lies in eternal abiding.
translations.idiomatic: These are not the return — the return lies in eternal abiding.

sentences.zh: 常住之象，常道孰異？

translations.literal: The image of eternal abiding — how do the eternal Ways differ?
translations.idiomatic: As for the image of eternal abiding — how do the eternal Ways differ?

sentences.zh: 神仙有死，權便之說。

translations.literal: That immortals die is an expedient doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The claim that immortals die is an expedient teaching.

sentences.zh: 神仙是大化之總稱，非窮妙之至名。

translations.literal: Immortal is the general term for great transformation, not the ultimate name of utmost subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: "Immortal" is the general term for great transformation, not the ultimate name of utmost subtlety.

sentences.zh: 至名無名，其有名者二十七品，仙變成真，真變成神，或謂之聖，各有九品，品極則入空寂，無爲無名。

translations.literal: The ultimate name is nameless; those with names are twenty-seven grades — immortal transforms to true, true transforms to spirit, or is called sage; each has nine grades, and when grades reach their limit one enters empty silence, non-action, and namelessness.
translations.idiomatic: The ultimate name is nameless; those with names are twenty-seven grades — immortal transforms to true, true transforms to spirit, or is called sage; each has nine grades, and when grades reach their limit one enters empty silence, non-action, and namelessness.

sentences.zh: 若服食茹芝，延壽萬億，壽盡則死，藥極則枯，此修考之士，非神仙之流也。

translations.literal: If one ingests elixirs and eats fungus to extend life for billions of years, when life is exhausted one still dies, and when medicine reaches its limit it withers — these are cultivation and examination scholars, not of the immortal stream.
translations.idiomatic: If one ingests elixirs and eats fungus to extend life for billions of years, when life is exhausted one still dies, and when medicine reaches its limit it withers — these are cultivation and examination scholars, not of the immortal stream.

sentences.zh: 明僧紹《正二教論》以爲「佛明其宗，老全其生。

translations.literal: Ming Sengshao's "Correcting the Two Teachings Essay" holds that "the Buddha clarifies its school, and Laozi preserves life completely.
translations.idiomatic: Ming Sengshao's Correcting the Two Teachings Essay holds that "the Buddha clarifies its school, and Laozi preserves life completely.

sentences.zh: 守生者蔽，明宗者通。

translations.literal: Preserving life is blind; clarifying the school is penetrating.
translations.idiomatic: Preserving life is blind; clarifying the school is penetrating.

sentences.zh: 今道家稱長生不死，名補天曹，大乖老、莊立言本理」。

translations.literal: Now Daoists call immortality without death and title it filling the heavenly registers — greatly deviating from the foundational principle of Laozi and Zhuangzi's teaching."
translations.idiomatic: Now Daoists speak of immortality without death and call it filling the heavenly registers — greatly deviating from the foundational principle of Laozi and Zhuangzi's teaching."

sentences.zh: 文惠太子、竟陵王子良竝好釋法。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wen Hui and Jiling Prince Ziliang both loved Buddhist dharma.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui and Jiling Prince Xiao Ziliang both loved Buddhist dharma.

sentences.zh: 吳興孟景翼爲道士，太子召入玄圃園。

translations.literal: Meng Jingyi of Wuxing was a Daoist; the crown prince summoned him to the Xuanyuan Garden.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jingyi of Wuxing was a Daoist; the crown prince summoned him to the Xuanyuan Garden.

sentences.zh: 衆僧大會，子良使景翼禮佛，景翼不肯，子良送《十地經》與之。

translations.literal: At a great assembly of monks, Ziliang had Jingyi bow to the Buddha; Jingyi refused, and Ziliang sent him the Dasabhumi Sutra.
translations.idiomatic: At a great assembly of monks, Ziliang had Jingyi bow to the Buddha; Jingyi refused, and Ziliang sent him the Dasabhumi Sutra.

sentences.zh: 景翼造《正一論》。

translations.literal: Jingyi composed the "Correct One Essay."
translations.idiomatic: Jingyi composed the Correct One Essay.

sentences.zh: 大略曰：「《寶積》云『佛以一音廣說法』。

translations.literal: The summary says: "The Maharatnakuta says, 'The Buddha with one sound broadly expounds the dharma.'
translations.idiomatic: The summary says: "The Maharatnakuta Sutra says, 'The Buddha with one sound broadly expounds the dharma.'

sentences.zh: 老子云『聖人抱一以爲天下式』。

translations.literal: Laozi says, 'The sage embraces the One as the model for all under Heaven.'
translations.idiomatic: Laozi says, 'The sage embraces the One as the model for all under Heaven.'

sentences.zh: 『一』之爲妙，空玄絕於有境，神化贍於無窮，爲萬物而無爲，處一數而無數，莫之能名，強號爲一。

translations.literal: The wonder of the 'One' is empty and mysterious, transcending the realm of being; divine transformation suffices in the infinite; acting for the ten thousand things yet non-acting, dwelling in one number yet numberless — none can name it, so it is forcibly styled the One.
translations.idiomatic: The wonder of the 'One' is empty and mysterious, transcending the realm of being; divine transformation suffices in the infinite; acting for the ten thousand things yet non-acting, dwelling in one number yet numberless — none can name it, so it is forcibly styled the One.

sentences.zh: 在佛曰『實相』，在道曰『玄牝』。

translations.literal: In the Buddha it is called 'true mark'; in the Way it is called 'mysterious female.'
translations.idiomatic: In Buddhism it is called 'true mark'; in the Way it is called 'mysterious female.'

sentences.zh: 道之大象，卽佛之法身。

translations.literal: The Way's great image is precisely the Buddha's dharma body.
translations.idiomatic: The Way's great image is precisely the Buddha's dharma body.

sentences.zh: 以不守之守守法身，以不執之執執大象。

translations.literal: With non-guarding guard one guards the dharma body; with non-grasping grasp one grasps the great image.
translations.idiomatic: With non-guarding guard one guards the dharma body; with non-grasping grasp one grasps the great image.

sentences.zh: 但物有八萬四千行，說有八萬四千法。

translations.literal: But things have eighty-four thousand practices, and teachings have eighty-four thousand laws.
translations.idiomatic: But things have eighty-four thousand practices, and teachings have eighty-four thousand laws.

sentences.zh: 法乃至於無數，行亦逮於無央。

translations.literal: Laws extend to numberlessness, and practices reach to boundlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Laws extend to numberlessness, and practices reach to boundlessness.

sentences.zh: 等級隨緣，須導歸一。

translations.literal: Grades follow conditions, yet all must be guided back to the One.
