translations.idiomatic: Grades follow conditions, yet all must be guided back to the One.

sentences.zh: 歸一曰回向，向正卽無邪。

translations.literal: Return to the One is called 'turning toward'; turning toward the correct then there is no evil.
translations.idiomatic: Return to the One is called 'turning toward'; turning toward the correct then there is no evil.

sentences.zh: 邪觀旣遣，億善日新。

translations.literal: Evil views already dismissed, billions of merits are renewed day by day.
translations.idiomatic: Once evil views are dismissed, countless merits are renewed day by day.

sentences.zh: 三五四六，隨用而施。

translations.literal: Three, five, four, and six — applied as needed.
translations.idiomatic: Three, five, four, and six — applied as needed.

sentences.zh: 獨立不改，絕學無憂。

translations.literal: Stand alone unchanged; cease learning without worry.
translations.idiomatic: Stand alone unchanged; cease learning without worry.

sentences.zh: 曠劫諸聖，共遵斯『一』。

translations.literal: Sages across vast kalpas all follow this 'One.'
translations.idiomatic: Sages across vast kalpas all follow this 'One.'

sentences.zh: 老、釋未始於嘗分，迷者分之而未合。

translations.literal: Laozi and the Buddha were never from the beginning divided; the deluded divide them but have not united.
translations.idiomatic: Laozi and the Buddha were never from the beginning divided; the deluded divide them but have not united.

sentences.zh: 億善徧修，修徧成聖，雖十號千稱，終不能盡。

translations.literal: Billions of merits universally cultivated — when cultivation is complete one becomes a sage; though there are ten titles and a thousand names, ultimately they cannot be exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Cultivating countless merits throughout — when cultivation is complete one becomes a sage; though there are ten titles and a thousand names, ultimately they cannot be exhausted.

sentences.zh: 終不能盡，豈可思議。

translations.literal: Ultimately they cannot be exhausted — how can this be conceived?
translations.idiomatic: Ultimately they cannot be exhausted — how can this be conceived?

sentences.zh: 」司徒從事中郎張融作門律云：「道之與佛，逗極無二。

translations.literal: " Attendant Gentleman Zhang Rong of the Grand Steward wrote Gate Rules saying: "The Way and the Buddha, arriving at the ultimate, are without two.
translations.idiomatic: " Attendant Gentleman Zhang Rong of the Grand Steward wrote Gate Rules saying: "The Way and the Buddha, arriving at the ultimate, are without two.

sentences.zh: 吾見道士與道人戰儒墨，道人與道士獄是非。

translations.literal: I see Daoists and Buddhist masters battling Confucian and Mohist doctrines, and Buddhist masters and Daoists wrangling over right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: I see Daoists and Buddhist masters battling Confucian and Mohist doctrines, and Buddhist masters and Daoists wrangling over right and wrong.

sentences.zh: 昔有鴻飛天首，積遠難亮。

translations.literal: Once a swan flew at heaven's head, and accumulated distance made it hard to discern.
translations.idiomatic: Once a swan flew at heaven's head, and accumulated distance made it hard to discern.

sentences.zh: 越人以爲鳧，楚人以爲乙，人自楚越，鴻常一耳。

translations.literal: The people of Yue thought it a duck, and the people of Chu thought it the character yi; people differ between Chu and Yue, but the swan is always one.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Yue took it for a duck, and the people of Chu took it for the character yi — people differ between Chu and Yue, but the swan is always one.

sentences.zh: 」以示太子僕周顒。

translations.literal: " He showed this to Palace Supervisor Zhou Yong.
translations.idiomatic: " He showed this to Palace Supervisor Zhou Yong.

sentences.zh: 顒難之曰：「虛無法性，其寂雖同，位寂之方，其旨則別。

translations.literal: Yong challenged it, saying: "Void and dharma-nature — their silence is the same, but the position of silence differs, and their intent differs.
translations.idiomatic: Yong challenged it, saying: "Void and dharma-nature — their silence is the same, but the position of silence differs, and their intent differs.

sentences.zh: 論所謂『逗極無二』者，爲逗極於虛無，當無二於法性耶？

translations.literal: What your essay calls 'arriving at the ultimate without two' — if one arrives at the ultimate in void, should one not be without two in dharma-nature?
translations.idiomatic: What your essay calls 'arriving at the ultimate without two' — if one arrives at the ultimate in void, should one not be without two in dharma-nature?

sentences.zh: 足下所宗之本一物爲鴻乙耳。

translations.literal: The root of your honored stance is merely the one thing called swan-yi.
translations.idiomatic: The root of what you revere is merely the one thing seen as duck or yi — a swan.

sentences.zh: 驅馳佛道，無免二末。

translations.literal: Racing through the Buddha-Way, one cannot escape two branches.
translations.idiomatic: Racing through the Buddha-Way, one cannot escape two branches.

sentences.zh: 未知高鑒緣何識本，輕而宗之，其有旨乎？

translations.literal: I do not know on what basis your lofty insight recognizes the root and lightly reveres it — is there meaning in this?
translations.idiomatic: I do not know on what basis your lofty insight recognizes the root and lightly reveres it — is there meaning in this?

sentences.zh: 」往復文多不載。

translations.literal: " The back-and-forth texts are mostly not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: " The back-and-forth texts are mostly not recorded.

sentences.zh: 歡口不辯，善於著筆。

translations.literal: Huan's mouth was not eloquent, but he was skilled at writing.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Huan was not eloquent in speech, but he was skilled with the pen.

sentences.zh: 著《三名論》，甚工，鍾會《四本》之流也。

translations.literal: He wrote the "Three Names Essay," which was very accomplished — in the line of Zhong Hui's "Four Foundations."
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Three Names Essay, which was very accomplished — in the line of Zhong Hui's Four Foundations.

sentences.zh: 又注王弼《易》二《繫》，學者傳之。

translations.literal: He also annotated Wang Bi's two Appended Texts to the Changes, and scholars transmitted his work.
translations.idiomatic: He also annotated Wang Bi's two Appended Texts to the Changes, and scholars transmitted his work.

sentences.zh: 始興人盧度，亦有道術。

translations.literal: Lu Du of Shixing also possessed Daoist techniques.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Du of Shixing also possessed Daoist techniques.

sentences.zh: 少隨張永北征。

translations.literal: In youth he followed Zhang Yong on the northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In youth he followed Zhang Yong on the northern campaign.

sentences.zh: 永敗，虜追急，阻淮水不得過。

translations.literal: Yong was defeated, the enemy pursuit was urgent, and he was blocked at the Huai River and unable to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was defeated, the enemy pursuit was urgent, and he was blocked at the Huai River and unable to cross.

sentences.zh: 度心誓曰：「若得免死，從今不復殺生。

translations.literal: Du vowed in his heart, saying: "If I escape death, from now on I shall never again kill living beings.
translations.idiomatic: Du vowed in his heart, saying: "If I escape death, from now on I shall never again kill living beings.

sentences.zh: 」須臾見兩楯流來，接之得過。

translations.literal: " In a moment he saw two shields float by; he took hold of them and crossed.
translations.idiomatic: " In a moment he saw two shields float by; he took hold of them and crossed.

sentences.zh: 後隱居西昌三顧山，鳥獸隨之。

translations.literal: Later he lived in seclusion on Sangu Mountain in Xichang, and birds and beasts followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Later he lived in seclusion on Sangu Mountain in Xichang, and birds and beasts followed him.

sentences.zh: 夜有鹿觸其壁，度曰：「汝壞我壁。

translations.literal: One night a deer bumped his wall, and Du said: "You are ruining my wall.
translations.idiomatic: One night a deer bumped his wall, and Du said: "You are ruining my wall.

sentences.zh: 」鹿應聲去。

translations.literal: " The deer departed at the sound.
translations.idiomatic: " The deer departed at the sound.

sentences.zh: 屋前有池養魚，皆名呼之，魚次第來，取食乃去。

translations.literal: Before his house was a pond where he kept fish; he called each by name, and the fish came in order, took food, and then left.
translations.idiomatic: Before his house was a pond where he kept fish; he called each by name, and the fish came in order, took food, and then left.

sentences.zh: 逆知死年月，與親友別。

translations.literal: He foreknew the year and month of his death and bade farewell to kin and friends.
translations.idiomatic: He foreknew the year and month of his death and bade farewell to kin and friends.

sentences.zh: 永明末，以壽終。

translations.literal: In the late Yongming era, he died of natural causes.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Yongming era, he died of natural causes.

sentences.zh: 初，永明三年，徵驃騎參軍顧惠胤爲司徒主簿。

translations.literal: Initially, in the third year of Yongming, Cavalry General Staff Officer Gu Huiyin was summoned as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, in the third year of Yongming, Cavalry General Staff Officer Gu Huiyin was summoned to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward.

sentences.zh: 惠胤，宋鎮軍將軍覬之弟子也。

translations.literal: Huiyin was a disciple of Song General Who Pacifies the Army Gu Yizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Huiyin was a disciple of Song General Who Pacifies the Army Gu Yizhi.

sentences.zh: 閑居養志，不應徵辟。

translations.literal: He lived in retirement cultivating his will and did not respond to summons.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in quiet retirement, cultivating his aspirations, and declined the summons.

sentences.zh: 臧榮緒

translations.literal: Zang Rongxu
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu

sentences.zh: 臧榮緒，東莞莒人也。

translations.literal: Zang Rongxu was a native of Ju in Dongguan.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Rongxu was a native of Ju in Dongguan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖奉先，建陵令，父庸民，國子助教。

translations.literal: His grandfather Fengxian was Magistrate of Jianling; his father Yongmin was an Erudite at the National University.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Fengxian served as Magistrate of Jianling; his father Yongmin was an Erudite at the National University.

sentences.zh: 榮緒幼孤，躬自灌園，以供祭祀。

translations.literal: Rongxu was orphaned in youth; he personally tended the garden to supply sacrificial offerings.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned in youth, Rongxu personally tended the garden to supply offerings for ancestral rites.

sentences.zh: 母喪後，乃著《嫡寢論》，掃灑堂宇，置筵席，朔望輙拜薦，甘珍未嘗先食。

translations.literal: After his mother's death, he composed the "Treatise on the Principal Chamber," swept and cleaned the hall, set out mats and seats, and at the new and full moons invariably offered homage and tribute; delicacies he never tasted first.
translations.idiomatic: After his mother's death, he composed the "Treatise on the Principal Chamber," swept the hall clean, laid out mats and seats, and at every new and full moon unfailingly offered homage and tribute; never once did he taste delicacies before presenting them.

sentences.zh: 純篤好學，括東西晉爲一書，紀、錄、志、傳百一十卷。

translations.literal: Sincere and devoted, fond of learning, he gathered the Eastern and Western Jin into one work — annals, records, treatises, and biographies in one hundred ten scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Sincere and devoted, a dedicated scholar, he gathered the Eastern and Western Jin dynasties into a single history — annals, records, treatises, and biographies in one hundred and ten scrolls.

sentences.zh: 隱居京口教授。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion at Jingkou and taught.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion at Jingkou, where he taught.

sentences.zh: 南徐州辟西曹，舉秀才，不就。

translations.literal: Southern Xuzhou summoned him to the Western Section; he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Xuzhou summoned him to the Western Section; he was recommended as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate but declined.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲揚州，徵榮緒爲主簿，不到。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was governor of Yangzhou, he summoned Rongxu as Chief Clerk; he did not come.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was governor of Yangzhou, he summoned Rongxu to serve as Chief Clerk; Rongxu did not come.

sentences.zh: 司徒褚淵少時嘗命駕尋之。

translations.literal: Grand Steward Chu Yuan, in his youth, once ordered his carriage to seek him out.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Steward Chu Yuan, in his youth, once had his carriage sent to find him.

sentences.zh: 建元中，啟太祖曰：「榮緒，朱方隱者。

translations.literal: During the Jianyuan era, [Chu] submitted a memorial to the Founding Emperor, saying: "Rongxu is a recluse of Zhufang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianyuan era, Chu submitted a memorial to the Founding Emperor, saying: "Rongxu is a recluse of Zhufang.

sentences.zh: 昔臧質在宋，以國戚出牧彭岱，引爲行佐，非其所好，謝疾求免。

translations.literal: Formerly, when Zang Zhi was in Song, as a kin of the imperial house he went out to govern Peng and Dai, and took [Rongxu] on as a traveling staff officer; it was not to Rongxu's liking, and he cited illness to seek release.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly, when Zang Zhi held office in Song, a kinsman of the imperial house sent out to govern Peng and Dai, he took Rongxu on as a traveling staff officer; it was not to Rongxu's liking, and he cited illness to seek release.

sentences.zh: 蓬廬守志，漏濕是安，灌蔬終老。

translations.literal: In a thatched hut he kept his resolve; leaky and damp though it was, he found it sufficient; watering vegetables, he lived out his days.
translations.idiomatic: In a thatched hut he kept his resolve; leaky and damp though it was, he found it sufficient; tending his vegetable garden, he lived out his days.

sentences.zh: 與友關康之沈深典素，追古著書，撰《晉史》十袠，贊論雖無逸才，亦足彌綸一代。

translations.literal: With his friend Guan Kangzhi — profound, dignified, and plain — he traced antiquity in writing books, compiling the Jin History in ten fascicles; though the laudatory essays lacked outstanding talent, they sufficed to span a generation.
translations.idiomatic: With his friend Guan Kangzhi — profound, dignified, and plain — he turned to antiquity in his writing, compiling the Jin History in ten fascicles; though the laudatory essays lacked outstanding brilliance, they sufficed to span a generation.

sentences.zh: 臣歲時往京口，早與之遇。

translations.literal: Your subject, season by season, goes to Jingkou and long ago met him there.
translations.idiomatic: Your subject visits Jingkou season by season and met him there long ago.

sentences.zh: 近報其取書，始方送出，庶得備錄渠閣，採異甄善。

translations.literal: Recently it was reported that he is taking up his books; he has only just begun to send them out; I hope they may be fully recorded in the imperial archive, gathering the unusual and selecting the excellent.
translations.idiomatic: I have lately heard that he is gathering his books and has only just begun to send them out; I hope they may be fully recorded in the imperial archive, gathering what is uncommon and selecting what is finest.

sentences.zh: 」上答曰：「公所道臧榮緒者，吾甚志之。

translations.literal: " The emperor replied: "This Zang Rongxu of whom you speak — I am keenly mindful of him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor replied: "This Zang Rongxu of whom you speak — I have been keenly mindful of him.

sentences.zh: 其有史翰，欲令入天祿，甚佳。」

translations.literal: If he has historical writings, to have them enter the Heaven's Endowment [Archive] would be excellent."
translations.idiomatic: If he has historical writings, to have them enter the Archive of Heaven's Endowment would be excellent."

sentences.zh: 榮緒惇愛五經，謂人曰：「昔呂尚奉丹書，武王致齋降位，李、釋教誡，竝有禮敬之儀。

translations.literal: Rongxu cherished the Five Classics with deep devotion, saying to people: "Formerly Lü Shang received the cinnabar scroll, and King Wu observed fasting and lowered his seat; the teachings of Laozi and the Buddha both have rituals of respect.
translations.idiomatic: Rongxu cherished the Five Classics with deep devotion, saying to others: "Formerly Lü Shang received the cinnabar scroll, and King Wu observed fasting and lowered his seat; the teachings of Laozi and the Buddha both have their rituals of respect.

sentences.zh: 因甄明至道，乃著拜《五經序論》。

translations.literal: Accordingly, to clarify the supreme Way, he composed the "Treatise on Bowing to the Prefaces of the Five Classics."
translations.idiomatic: Accordingly, to clarify the supreme Way, he composed the "Treatise on Bowing to the Prefaces of the Five Classics."

sentences.zh: 常以宣尼生庚子日，陳《五經》拜之。

translations.literal: He regularly, on the day of Kongzi's birth in the gengzi cycle, arrayed the Five Classics and bowed to them.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of Confucius's birth — a gengzi day — he regularly arrayed the Five Classics and bowed to them.

sentences.zh: 自號「被褐先生」。

translations.literal: He styled himself "Master Clad in Coarse Cloth."
translations.idiomatic: He styled himself "Master Clad in Coarse Cloth."

sentences.zh: 又以飲酒亂德，言常爲誡。

translations.literal: He also held that wine disorders virtue, and this saying was often his admonition.
translations.idiomatic: He also held that wine disorders virtue, and this saying was his constant admonition.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongming, he died.

sentences.zh: 年七十四。

translations.literal: He was seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: He was seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 初，榮緒與關康之俱隱在京口，世號爲「二隱」。

translations.literal: Initially, Rongxu and Guan Kangzhi both lived in seclusion at Jingkou, and the age called them "the Two Recluses."
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Rongxu and Guan Kangzhi both lived in seclusion at Jingkou, and their contemporaries called them "the Two Recluses."

sentences.zh: 康之字伯愉，河東人。

translations.literal: Kangzhi, courtesy name Boyu, was a man of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Kangzhi, courtesy name Boyu, was a man of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 世居丹徒。

translations.literal: His family had long resided in Dantu.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in Dantu.

sentences.zh: 以墳籍爲務。

translations.literal: He made classical texts his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: He devoted himself to classical texts.

sentences.zh: 四十年不出門。

translations.literal: For forty years he did not go out his door.
translations.idiomatic: For forty years he never left his door.

sentences.zh: 不應州府辟。

translations.literal: He did not respond to summons from prefecture or province.
translations.idiomatic: He did not respond to summons from prefecture or province.

sentences.zh: 宋太始中，徵通直郎，不就。

translations.literal: In Song's Taishi era, he was summoned as Direct Attendant but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era of Song, he was summoned to serve as Direct Attendant but declined.

sentences.zh: 晚以母老家貧，求爲嶺南小縣。

translations.literal: Late in life, because his mother was aged and his family poor, he sought appointment to a small county in Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Late in life, his mother being aged and his family poor, he sought appointment to a small county in Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 性清約，獨處一室，稀與妻子相見。

translations.literal: By nature abstemious and plain, he dwelt alone in one room and rarely saw wife or children.
translations.idiomatic: Abstemious and plain by nature, he dwelt alone in a single room and rarely saw his wife or children.

sentences.zh: 不通賔客。

translations.literal: He did not receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: He received no guests.

sentences.zh: 弟子以業傳受。

translations.literal: His disciples received and transmitted his learning.
translations.idiomatic: His disciples received and transmitted his learning.

sentences.zh: 尤善《左氏春秋》。

translations.literal: He was especially skilled in the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: He was especially skilled in the Zuo Tradition to the Spring and Autumn Annals.

sentences.zh: 太祖爲領軍，素好此學，送《春秋五經》，康之手自點定，幷得論禮記十餘條。

translations.literal: When the Founding Emperor was Commandant-in-Chief, he had long favored this learning and sent the Five Classics with the Spring and Autumn; Kangzhi personally collated and corrected them, and also produced more than ten entries discussing the Record of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When the Founding Emperor was Commandant-in-Chief, he had long favored this learning and sent the Five Classics with the Spring and Autumn; Kangzhi personally collated and corrected them, and also produced more than ten entries discussing the Record of Rites.

sentences.zh: 上甚悅，寶愛之。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased and treasured them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly pleased and treasured them.

sentences.zh: 遺詔以經本入玄宮。

translations.literal: By his testamentary decree, the scriptural copies entered the Mysterious Palace.
translations.idiomatic: By his testamentary decree, the scriptural copies were deposited in the Mysterious Palace.

sentences.zh: 宋末卒。

translations.literal: He died near the end of Song.
translations.idiomatic: He died near the end of Song.

sentences.zh: 何求字子有，廬江灊人也。

translations.literal: He Qiu, courtesy name Ziyou, was a native of Qian in Lujiang.
translations.idiomatic: He Qiu, courtesy name Ziyou, was a native of Qian in Lujiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖尚之，宋司空，父鑠，宜都太守。

translations.literal: His grandfather Shangzhi was Song Minister of Works; his father Shuo was Administrator of Yidu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Shangzhi served as Minister of Works under Song; his father Shuo served as Administrator of Yidu.

sentences.zh: 求元嘉末爲宋文帝挽郎，解褐著作郎，中軍衞軍行佐，太子舍人，平南參軍，撫軍主簿，太子洗馬，丹陽、吳郡丞。

translations.literal: Qiu, at the end of Yuanjia, served as a Mourning Officer for Emperor Wen of Song; upon removing his hemp cloth he became a Drafting Secretary, staff officer to the Guard General and Central Army, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent, Adjutant to the General Who Pacifies the South, Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Insurrection, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Assistant Administrator of Danyang and Wu commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Yuanjia era, Qiu served as a Mourning Officer for Emperor Wen of Song; upon entering official life he became a Drafting Secretary, staff officer to the Guard General and Central Army, Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent, Adjutant to the General Who Pacifies the South, Chief Clerk to the General Who Pacifies the Insurrection, Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household, and Assistant Administrator of Danyang and Wu commanderies.

sentences.zh: 清退無嗜欲。

translations.literal: Pure and retiring, without cravings.
translations.idiomatic: Pure and retiring, without cravings or attachments.

sentences.zh: 又除征北參軍事，司徒主簿，太子中舍人。

translations.literal: He was further appointed Staff Officer to the General Who Campaigns North, Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward, and Central Attendant to the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was further appointed Staff Officer to the General Who Campaigns North, Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward, and Central Attendant to the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 泰始中，妻亡，還吳葬舊墓，除中書郎，不拜。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era, his wife died; he returned to Wu to bury her in the family tomb; he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era, after his wife died, he returned to Wu to bury her in the family tomb; he was appointed Secretariat Gentleman but declined.

sentences.zh: 仍住吳，居波若寺，足不踰戶，人莫見其面。

translations.literal: He continued to dwell in Wu, residing at the Prajna Temple; his feet never crossed the threshold, and no one saw his face.
translations.idiomatic: He continued to dwell in Wu, residing at the Prajna Temple; his feet never crossed the threshold, and no one saw his face.

sentences.zh: 明帝崩，出奔國哀，除爲司空從事中郎，不就。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming died, he came out to join the national mourning; he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Minister of Works but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, he came out to join the national mourning; he was appointed Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Minister of Works but declined.

sentences.zh: 乃除永嘉太守。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Administrator of Yongjia.
translations.idiomatic: He was then appointed Administrator of Yongjia.

sentences.zh: 求時寄住南澗寺，不肯詣臺，乞於寺拜受，見許。

translations.literal: Qiu was then staying at the Southern Stream Temple; he refused to go to the capital, begged to receive the appointment at the temple, and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu was then staying at the Southern Stream Temple; he refused to go to the capital, begged to receive the appointment at the temple, and permission was granted.

sentences.zh: 一夜忽乘小船逃歸吳，隱虎丘山，復除黃門郎，不就。

translations.literal: One night he suddenly took a small boat and fled back to Wu, hiding on Tiger Hill; he was again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: One night he suddenly took a small boat and fled back to Wu, hiding on Tiger Hill; he was again appointed Gentleman at the Yellow Gate but declined.

sentences.zh: 永明四年，世祖以爲太中大夫，又不就。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongming, the Shizu Emperor made him Grand Master of the Palace but he again did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongming, the Shizu Emperor made him Grand Master of the Palace, but he again declined.

sentences.zh: 七年，卒。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十六。

translations.literal: He was fifty-six.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 初，求母王氏爲父所害，求兄弟以此無宦情。

translations.literal: Initially, Qiu's mother the Lady Wang was killed by his father; Qiu and his brothers for this reason had no desire for office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Qiu's mother, Lady Wang, had been killed by his father; for this reason Qiu and his brothers had no desire for office.

sentences.zh: 點弟胤，有儒術，亦懷隱遁之志。

translations.literal: Dian's younger brother Yin had Confucian learning and also harbored the resolve to withdraw in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Dian's younger brother Yin had Confucian learning and also harbored the resolve to withdraw in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 所居宅名爲小山。

translations.literal: The residence where he lived was called Little Hill.
translations.idiomatic: The residence where he lived was called Little Hill.

sentences.zh: 隆昌中，爲中書令，以皇后從叔見親寵。

translations.literal: In the Longchang era, he became Director of the Secretariat; as the empress's maternal uncle he was treated with intimate favor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Longchang era, he became Director of the Secretariat; as the empress's maternal uncle he was treated with intimate favor.

sentences.zh: 明帝卽位，胤賣園宅，將遂本志。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Yin sold his gardens and residence, intending to fulfill his original resolve.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, Yin sold his gardens and residence, intending to fulfill his original resolve.

sentences.zh: 建武四年，爲散騎常侍、巴陵王師。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, he became Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders and Tutor to the Prince of Baling.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Jianwu, he became Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders and Tutor to the Prince of Baling.

sentences.zh: 聞吳興太守謝朏致仕，慮後之，於是奉表不待報而去，隱會稽山。

translations.literal: Hearing that Xie Tiao, Administrator of Wuxing, had retired, fearing he would be left behind, he thereupon submitted a memorial and, without awaiting reply, departed, hiding on Mount Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Xie Tiao, Administrator of Wuxing, had retired, anxious not to be left behind, he submitted a memorial and, without awaiting reply, departed to hide on Mount Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 上大怒，令有司奏彈胤，然發優詔焉。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered the relevant offices to impeach Yin, yet issued an excellent edict [praising him].
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was greatly angered and ordered the relevant offices to impeach Yin, yet issued an edict commending him nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，徵散騎常侍，太常卿。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan, he was summoned to serve as Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders and Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 劉虯字靈預，南陽涅陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu You, courtesy name Lingyu, was a native of Niyang in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liu You, courtesy name Lingyu, was a native of Niyang in Nanyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 舊族，徙居江陵。

translations.literal: An old clan, they moved and settled in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: An old clan, they had moved and settled in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 虯少而抗節好學，須得祿便隱。

translations.literal: You from youth was upright in principle and fond of learning; once he had secured a salary, he withdrew in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: From youth You was upright in principle and fond of learning; once he had secured a salary, he withdrew in seclusion.

sentences.zh: 宋泰始中，仕至晉平王驃騎記室，當陽令。

translations.literal: In Song's Taishi era, he served up to Staff Secretary to the Cavalry General of the Prince of Jinping, and Magistrate of Dangyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taishi era of Song, he served up to Staff Secretary to the Cavalry General of the Prince of Jinping and as Magistrate of Dangyang.

sentences.zh: 罷官歸家，靜處斷穀，餌朮及胡麻。

translations.literal: Leaving office he returned home, dwelt in quiet, abstained from grain, and took atractylodes and sesame as food.
translations.idiomatic: Leaving office he returned home, dwelt in quiet, abstained from grain, and subsisted on atractylodes and sesame.

sentences.zh: 建元初，豫章王爲荊州，教辟虯爲別駕，與同郡宗測、新野庾易竝遣書禮請，虯等各修牋答，而不應辟命。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan, the Prince of Yuzhang was governor of Jingzhou and by order summoned You as Administrator Assistant; together with Zong Ce of the same commandery and Yu Yi of Xinye he sent letters of invitation with ritual courtesy; You and the others each composed reply notes but did not respond to the summons.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianyuan, when the Prince of Yuzhang was governor of Jingzhou, he summoned You to serve as Administrator Assistant; together with Zong Ce of the same commandery and Yu Yi of Xinye, he sent letters of invitation with full ritual courtesy; You and the others each composed reply notes but did not accept the summons.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，刺史廬陵王子卿表虯及同郡宗測、宗尚之、庾易、劉昭五人，請加蒲車束帛之命。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, the Inspector, the Prince of Luling Ziqing, memorialized concerning You, Zong Ce, Zong Shangzhi, Yu Yi, and Liu Zhao — five men of the same commandery — requesting that they be granted the appointment of envoy's carriage with silks and cloth.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming, the Inspector, Prince Ziqing of Luling, memorialized concerning You, Zong Ce, Zong Shangzhi, Yu Yi, and Liu Zhao — five men of the same commandery — requesting that they be granted the honor of an envoy's carriage with silks and cloth.

sentences.zh: 詔徵爲通直郎，不就。

translations.literal: An edict summoned him as Direct Attendant; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: An edict summoned him to serve as Direct Attendant; he declined.

sentences.zh: 竟陵王子良致書通意。

translations.literal: Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, sent a letter expressing his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, sent a letter expressing his intent.

sentences.zh: 虯答曰：「虯四節卧病，三時營灌，暢餘陰於山澤，託暮情於魚鳥，寧非唐、虞重恩，周、邵宏施？

translations.literal: You replied: "You lies ill through the four seasons, tends irrigation in three seasons, enjoys lingering shade in mountains and marshes, and entrusts twilight feelings to fish and birds — is this not the heavy grace of Tang and Yu, the grand bestowal of the Zhou Dukes?
translations.idiomatic: You replied: "I lie ill through the four seasons and tend irrigation in three; I enjoy lingering shade in mountains and marshes and entrust twilight feelings to fish and birds — is this not the heavy grace of Tang and Yu, the grand bestowal of the Zhou dukes?

sentences.zh: 虯進不研機入玄，無洙泗稷館之辯；

translations.literal: Advancing, You does not investigate subtleties and enter the profound, and lacks the disputation of Zhu-Si and the Jiguan;
translations.idiomatic: Advancing, I do not investigate subtleties and enter the profound, and lack the disputation of the schools of Zhu and Si;

sentences.zh: 退不凝心出累，非冢間樹下之節。

translations.literal: Retreating, he does not concentrate mind and release burdens, and lacks the integrity of beneath the family tomb or beneath a tree.
translations.idiomatic: Retreating, I do not concentrate the mind and release worldly burden, and lack the integrity of one who dwells beneath the family tomb or beneath a tree.

sentences.zh: 遠澤旣灑，仁規先著。

translations.literal: Your distant gracious dew has already been sprinkled; humane rule is already manifest.
translations.idiomatic: Your distant gracious dew has already been sprinkled; humane rule is already manifest.

sentences.zh: 謹收樵牧之嫌，敬加軾躔之義。」

translations.literal: I respectfully accept the suspicion of woodcutter and herdsman, and reverently add the meaning of the chariot bar and reins."
translations.idiomatic: I respectfully accept the charge of being no more than woodcutter and herdsman, and reverently add the meaning of the chariot bar and reins."

sentences.zh: 虯精信釋氏，衣麤布衣，禮佛長齋。

translations.literal: You faithfully believed in the Shakya teaching, wore coarse hemp cloth, worshipped the Buddha and kept long fasts.
translations.idiomatic: You faithfully believed in the Buddha's teaching, wore coarse hemp cloth, worshipped the Buddha, and kept long fasts.

sentences.zh: 注《法華經》，自講佛義。

translations.literal: He annotated the Lotus Sutra and himself lectured on Buddhist meaning.
translations.idiomatic: He annotated the Lotus Sutra and himself lectured on Buddhist doctrine.

sentences.zh: 以江陵西沙洲去人遠，乃徙居之。

translations.literal: Because West Sandbar of Jiangling was far from people, he moved and dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: Because West Sandbar of Jiangling was far from human habitation, he moved and dwelt there.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，詔徵國子博士，不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, an edict summoned him as Erudite of the National University; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, an edict summoned him to serve as Erudite of the National University; he declined.

sentences.zh: 其冬虯病，正晝有白雲徘徊檐戶之內，又有香氣及磬聲，其日卒。

translations.literal: That winter You fell ill; at midday white clouds lingered within the eaves and doorway, and there were also fragrance and chime sounds; that day he died.
translations.idiomatic: That winter You fell ill; at midday white clouds lingered within the eaves and doorway, and there were also fragrance and the sound of chimes; that day he died.

sentences.zh: 年五十八。

translations.literal: He was fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 劉昭與虯同宗。

translations.literal: Liu Zhao was of the same clan as You.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhao was of the same clan as You.

sentences.zh: 州辟祭酒從事，不就。

translations.literal: The province summoned him as Staff Officer to the Libationer; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province summoned him to serve as Staff Officer to the Libationer; he declined.

sentences.zh: 隱居山中。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion in the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion in the mountains.

sentences.zh: 庾易字幼簡，新野新野人也。

translations.literal: Yu Yi, courtesy name Youjian, was a native of Xinye in Xinye [Commandery].
translations.idiomatic: Yu Yi, courtesy name Youjian, was a native of Xinye in Xinye Commandery.

sentences.zh: 徙居屬江陵。

translations.literal: They moved and settled, becoming subjects of Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: They moved and settled, becoming subjects of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 祖玫，巴郡太守，父道驥，安西參軍。

translations.literal: His grandfather Mei was Administrator of Ba Commandery; his father Daoqi was Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Mei served as Administrator of Ba Commandery; his father Daoqi served as Staff Officer to the General Who Pacifies the West.

sentences.zh: 易志性恬隱，不交外物。

translations.literal: Yi by nature and resolve was tranquil and retiring, and did not mingle with outward things.
translations.idiomatic: Tranquil and retiring by nature and resolve, Yi did not mingle with the world outside.

sentences.zh: 建元元年，刺史豫章王辟爲驃騎參軍，不就。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Inspector, the Prince of Yuzhang, summoned him as Cavalry General Staff Officer; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jianyuan, the Inspector, the Prince of Yuzhang, summoned him to serve as Cavalry General Staff Officer; he declined.

sentences.zh: 臨川王映臨州，獨重易，上表薦之，餉麥百斛。

translations.literal: When the Prince of Linchuan Ying came to the province, he alone valued Yi highly, submitted a memorial recommending him, and sent a gift of one hundred bushels of wheat.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Linchuan Ying came to the province, he alone valued Yi highly, submitted a memorial recommending him, and sent a gift of one hundred bushels of wheat.

sentences.zh: 易謂使人曰：「民樵採麋鹿之伍，終其解毛之衣，馳騁日月之車，得保自耕之祿，於大王之恩，亦已深矣。

translations.literal: Yi said to the messenger: "This commoner belongs among woodcutters and deer-hunters; to the end I wear deerskin clothes, drive the chariot of sun and moon, and secure the salary of self-cultivation — toward the great prince's grace, it is already deep enough.
translations.idiomatic: Yi said to the messenger: "This commoner belongs among woodcutters and deer-hunters; to the end I wear deerskin clothes, drive the chariot of sun and moon, and secure the salary of self-cultivation — toward the great prince's grace, it is already more than enough.

sentences.zh: 」辭不受。

translations.literal: " He declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He declined and did not accept.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，詔徵太子舍人，不就。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming, an edict summoned him to serve as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; he declined.

sentences.zh: 以文義自樂。

translations.literal: He took delight in literary meaning for himself.
translations.idiomatic: He took delight in literary learning for its own sake.

sentences.zh: 安西長史袁彖欽其風，通書致遺。

translations.literal: Yuan Can, Chief Secretary to the General Who Pacifies the West, admired his character and sent a letter with gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Can, Chief Secretary to the General Who Pacifies the West, admired his character and sent a letter with gifts.

sentences.zh: 易以連理机竹翹書格報之。

translations.literal: Yi replied with a linked-grain bamboo writing tablet bound with book clasps.
translations.idiomatic: Yi replied with a linked-grain bamboo writing tablet bound with ornamental book clasps.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，詔復徵爲司徒主簿，不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, an edict again summoned him as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, an edict again summoned him to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward; he declined.

sentences.zh: 卒。

translations.literal: He died.
translations.idiomatic: He died.

sentences.zh: 宗測字敬微，南陽人，宋徵士炳孫也。

translations.literal: Zong Ce, courtesy name Jingwei, was a man of Nanyang, grandson of Song's Recluse Bing.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ce, courtesy name Jingwei, was a man of Nanyang, grandson of the Song recluse Bing.

sentences.zh: 世居江陵。

translations.literal: His family had long resided in Jiangling.
translations.idiomatic: His family had long resided in Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 測少靜退，不樂人間。

translations.literal: Ce from youth was quiet and retiring, and did not delight in the human world.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Ce was quiet and retiring, and took no delight in worldly life.

sentences.zh: 歎曰：「家貧親老，不擇官而仕，先哲以爲美談，余竊有惑。

translations.literal: He sighed and said: "When one's family is poor and parents aged, taking office without choosing the post — former sages took this for fine talk, but I privately have doubts.
translations.idiomatic: He sighed and said: "When one's family is poor and one's parents aged, taking office without choosing the post — former sages held this up as fine talk, but I privately have my doubts.

sentences.zh: 誠不能潛感地金，冥致江鯉，但當用天道，分地利。

translations.literal: Truly one cannot secretly move earth's gold or in darkness obtain the river carp; one ought only to employ Heaven's Way and apportion earth's advantage.
translations.idiomatic: Truly one cannot secretly move earth's gold or in darkness obtain the river carp; one ought only to follow Heaven's Way and apportion earth's advantage.

sentences.zh: 孰能食人厚祿，憂人重事乎？」

translations.literal: Who can eat another's rich salary yet worry over his weighty affairs?"
translations.idiomatic: Who can eat another's rich salary yet bear the weight of his heavy affairs?"

sentences.zh: 州舉秀才，主簿，不就。

translations.literal: The province recommended him as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate and summoned him as Chief Clerk; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The province recommended him as a Filial and Incorrupt graduate and summoned him as Chief Clerk; he declined.

sentences.zh: 驃騎豫章王徵爲參軍，測答府召云：「何爲謬傷海鳥，橫斤山木？

translations.literal: The Cavalry General, the Prince of Yuzhang, summoned him as Staff Officer; Ce replied to the prefectural summons: "Why wrongly harm the seabird and wield the axe against mountain trees?
translations.idiomatic: The Cavalry General, the Prince of Yuzhang, summoned him to serve as Staff Officer; Ce replied to the prefectural summons: "Why wrongly harm the seabird and wield the axe against mountain trees?

sentences.zh: 」母喪，身負土植松柏。

translations.literal: " After his mother's death, he personally carried earth and planted pines and cypresses.
translations.idiomatic: " After his mother's death, he personally carried earth and planted pines and cypresses.

sentences.zh: 豫章王復遣書請之，辟爲參軍。

translations.literal: The Prince of Yuzhang again sent a letter inviting him and summoned him as Staff Officer.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Yuzhang again sent a letter inviting him and summoned him to serve as Staff Officer.

sentences.zh: 測答曰：「性同鱗羽，愛止山壑，眷戀松筠，輕迷人路。

translations.literal: Ce replied: "By nature I am like scales and feathers — my affection stops at mountains and valleys; I cherish pines and bamboo and lightly regard the path that leads men astray.
translations.idiomatic: Ce replied: "By nature I am like fish scales and bird feathers — my affection stops at mountains and valleys; I cherish pines and bamboo and hold lightly the path that draws men into the world.

sentences.zh: 縱宕巖流，有若狂者，忽不知老至，而今鬢已白，豈容課虛責有，限魚慕鳥哉！

translations.literal: Roaming recklessly on cliffs and streams like one possessed, suddenly I knew not that old age had come; and now my temples are white — how can I tolerate empty demands for what exists, confining fish that envy birds!
translations.idiomatic: Roaming recklessly on cliffs and streams like one possessed, I suddenly knew not that old age had come; and now my temples are white — how can I tolerate empty demands for what exists, confining a fish that envies birds!

sentences.zh: 」永明三年，詔徵太子舍人，不就。

translations.literal: " In the third year of Yongming, an edict summoned him as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " In the third year of Yongming, an edict summoned him to serve as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; he declined.

sentences.zh: 欲遊名山，乃寫祖炳所畫尚子平圖於壁上。

translations.literal: Wishing to roam famous mountains, he copied on the wall Zu Bing's painting of Shang Zizping.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to roam famous mountains, he copied on the wall his ancestor Bing's painting of Shang Zizping.

sentences.zh: 測長子宦在京師，知父此旨，便求祿還爲南郡丞，付以家事。

translations.literal: Ce's eldest son held office in the capital; knowing his father's intent, he sought a salary and returned as Assistant Administrator of Nan Commandery, entrusting him with family affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ce's eldest son held office in the capital; knowing his father's intent, he sought a post and returned as Assistant Administrator of Nan Commandery to take charge of family affairs.

sentences.zh: 刺史安陸王子敬、長史劉寅以下皆贈送之，測無所受。

translations.literal: The Inspector, the Prince of Anlu Zijing, the Chief Secretary Liu Yin, and those below all sent gifts; Ce accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: The Inspector, Prince Zijing of Anlu, the Chief Secretary Liu Yin, and others all sent gifts; Ce accepted none.

sentences.zh: 齎《老子》《莊子》二書自隨。

translations.literal: He carried with him the two books, the Laozi and the Zhuangzi.
translations.idiomatic: He carried with him only the Laozi and the Zhuangzi.

sentences.zh: 子孫拜辭悲泣，測長嘯不視，遂往廬山，止祖炳舊宅。

translations.literal: His descendants bowed in farewell and wept; Ce gave a long whistle and did not look back, then went to Mount Lu and lodged at Zu Bing's old residence.
translations.idiomatic: His descendants bowed in farewell and wept; Ce gave a long whistle and did not look back, then went to Mount Lu and lodged at his ancestor Bing's old residence.

sentences.zh: 魚復侯子響爲江州，厚遣贈遺。

translations.literal: Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, was governor of Jiangzhou and sent lavish gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Zixiang, Marquis of Yufu, was governor of Jiangzhou and sent lavish gifts.

sentences.zh: 測曰：「少有狂疾，尋山採藥，遠來至此。

translations.literal: Ce said: "From youth I have had a mad disorder; I seek mountains and gather herbs, and came from afar to this place.
translations.idiomatic: Ce said: "From youth I have had a mad disorder; I seek mountains and gather herbs, and came from afar to this place.

sentences.zh: 量腹而進松朮，度形而衣薜蘿，淡然已足，豈容當此橫施！

translations.literal: Measuring belly I take pine and atractylodes; measuring form I wear rushes and moss — plainly this is enough; how can I accept such imposition!"
translations.idiomatic: Measuring my belly I take pine and atractylodes; measuring my form I wear rushes and moss — plainly this is enough; how can I accept such an imposition!"

sentences.zh: 」子響命駕造之，測避不見。

translations.literal: " Zixiang ordered his carriage to visit him; Ce avoided him and did not meet.
translations.idiomatic: " Zixiang ordered his carriage to visit him; Ce avoided him and refused to meet.

sentences.zh: 後子響不告而來，奄至所住，測不得已，巾褐對之，竟不交言，子響不悅而退。

translations.literal: Later Zixiang came without announcement, suddenly arriving at his dwelling; Ce had no choice, and in headcloth and coarse cloth faced him but ultimately exchanged no words; Zixiang withdrew displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Later Zixiang came without announcement, suddenly arriving at his dwelling; Ce had no choice and, in headcloth and coarse cloth, faced him but exchanged no words; Zixiang withdrew displeased.

sentences.zh: 尚書令王儉餉測蒲褥。

translations.literal: Wang Jian, Director of the Secretariat, sent Ce a rush mat.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jian, Director of the Secretariat, sent Ce a rush mat.

sentences.zh: 頃之，測送弟喪還西，仍留舊宅永業寺，絕賔友，唯與同志庾易、劉虯、宗人尚之等往來講說。

translations.literal: Before long, Ce escorted his younger brother's coffin westward, then remained at the old residence, Yongye Temple, cutting off guests and friends; only with kindred spirits Yu Yi, Liu You, and clansman Shangzhi and others did he come and go in mutual discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Ce escorted his younger brother's coffin westward, then remained at the old residence at Yongye Temple, cutting off guests and friends; only with kindred spirits Yu Yi, Liu You, and clansman Shangzhi and others did he exchange visits and discourse.

sentences.zh: 刺史隨王子隆至鎮，遣別駕宗哲致勞問，測笑曰：「貴賤理隔，何以及此。

translations.literal: When the Inspector, the Prince of Sui Zilong, arrived at his post, he sent Administrator Assistant Zong Zhe to convey regards; Ce laughed and said: "Noble and base are separated by principle — how could it reach this far?
translations.idiomatic: When the Inspector, Prince Zilong of Sui, arrived at his post, he sent Administrator Assistant Zong Zhe to convey regards; Ce laughed and said: "Noble and base are separated by principle — how could it reach this far?

sentences.zh: 」竟不答。

translations.literal: " In the end he did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: " In the end he did not reply.

sentences.zh: 建武二年，徵爲司徒主簿，不就，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Jianwu, he was summoned as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward; he did not accept, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Jianwu, he was summoned to serve as Chief Clerk to the Grand Steward; he declined, and died.

sentences.zh: 測善畫，自圖阮籍遇蘇門於行障上，坐卧對之。

translations.literal: Ce was skilled at painting; he painted himself the scene of Ruan Ji meeting Sumen on a portable screen, and sat and lay facing it.
translations.idiomatic: Ce was skilled at painting; he painted on a portable screen the scene of Ruan Ji meeting Sumen, and sat and lay facing it.

sentences.zh: 又畫永業佛影臺，皆爲妙作。

translations.literal: He also painted the Buddha-shadow terrace at Yongye — all were masterworks.
translations.idiomatic: He also painted the Buddha-shadow terrace at Yongye — all were masterworks.

sentences.zh: 頗好音律，善《易老》，續皇甫謐《高士傳》三卷。

translations.literal: He was rather fond of music, skilled in the Changes and Laozi, and continued Huangfu Mi's Biographies of Exalted Worthies in three scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He was rather fond of music, skilled in the Changes and Laozi, and continued Huangfu Mi's Biographies of Exalted Worthies in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 又嘗遊衡山七嶺，著《衡山》、《廬山記》。

translations.literal: He also once roamed the seven peaks of Mount Heng and composed Records of Mount Heng and Mount Lu.
translations.idiomatic: He also once roamed the seven peaks of Mount Heng and composed Records of Mount Heng and Mount Lu.

sentences.zh: 尚之字敬文，亦好山澤。

translations.literal: Shangzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, also loved mountains and marshes.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi, courtesy name Jingwen, also loved mountains and marshes.

sentences.zh: 與劉虯俱以驃騎記室不仕。

translations.literal: Together with Liu You he declined office as Staff Secretary to the Cavalry General.
translations.idiomatic: Together with Liu You he declined office as Staff Secretary to the Cavalry General.

sentences.zh: 宋末，刺史武陵王辟贊府，豫章王辟別駕，竝不就。

translations.literal: Near the end of Song, the Inspector, the Prince of Wuling, summoned him to the praise office; the Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Administrator Assistant — both he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Song, the Inspector, the Prince of Wuling, summoned him to the praise office; the Prince of Yuzhang summoned him as Administrator Assistant — he declined both.

sentences.zh: 永明中，與劉虯同徵爲通直郎，和帝中興初，又徵爲諮議，竝不就。

translations.literal: During Yongming, together with Liu You he was summoned as Direct Attendant; at the beginning of the Restoration under Emperor He, he was again summoned as Adviser — both he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, together with Liu You he was summoned to serve as Direct Attendant; at the beginning of the Restoration under Emperor He, he was again summoned as Adviser — he declined both.

sentences.zh: 壽終。

translations.literal: He died at the end of his years.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the end of his years.

sentences.zh: 杜京產

translations.literal: Du Jingchan
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingchan

sentences.zh: 杜京產字景齊，吳郡錢唐人。

translations.literal: Du Jingchan, courtesy name Jingqi, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Du Jingchan, courtesy name Jingqi, was a man of Qiantang in Wu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 杜子恭玄孫也。

translations.literal: He was the great-great-grandson of Du Zigong.
translations.idiomatic: He was the great-great-grandson of Du Zigong.

sentences.zh: 祖運，爲劉毅衞軍參軍，父道鞠，州從事，善彈棋，世傳五斗米道，至京產及子栖。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yun served as Staff Officer to the Guard General of Liu Yi; his father Daoju was a provincial staff officer, skilled at pitch-pot; the family transmitted the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice from generation to generation, down to Jingchan and his son Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yun served as Staff Officer to the Guard General Liu Yi; his father Daoju was a provincial staff officer, skilled at pitch-pot; the family transmitted the Way of the Five Pecks of Rice from generation to generation, down to Jingchan and his son Qi.

sentences.zh: 京產少恬靜，閉意榮宦。

translations.literal: Jingchan from youth was tranquil and quiet, shutting off desire for glory and office.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jingchan was tranquil and quiet, shutting off all desire for glory and office.

sentences.zh: 頗涉文義，專修黃老。

translations.literal: He had considerable acquaintance with literary meaning and devoted himself exclusively to Huang-Lao learning.
translations.idiomatic: He had considerable acquaintance with literary learning and devoted himself exclusively to Huang-Lao teaching.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔覬，清剛有峻節，一見而爲款交。

translations.literal: Kong Yi of Kuaiji was pure, firm, and of lofty integrity; at one meeting they became warm friends.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Yi of Kuaiji was pure, firm, and of lofty integrity; at one meeting they became warm friends.

sentences.zh: 郡召主簿，州辟從事，稱疾去。

translations.literal: The commandery summoned him as Chief Clerk; the province summoned him as staff officer; he cited illness and left.
translations.idiomatic: The commandery summoned him as Chief Clerk; the province summoned him as staff officer; he cited illness and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 除奉朝請，不就。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant at Court Audience but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant at Court Audience but declined.

sentences.zh: 與同郡顧歡同契，始寧東山開舍授學。

translations.literal: With Gu Huan of the same commandery he shared a bond; on the Eastern Hill of Shining he opened a dwelling to teach.
translations.idiomatic: With Gu Huan of the same commandery he shared a deep bond; on the Eastern Hill of Shining he opened a dwelling to teach.

sentences.zh: 建元中，武陵王曄爲會稽，太祖遣儒士劉瓛入東爲曄講說，京產請瓛至山舍講書，傾資供待，子栖躬自屣履，爲瓛生徒下食，其禮賢如此。

translations.literal: During Jianyuan, the Prince of Wuling Ye was governor of Kuaiji; the Founding Emperor sent the Confucian Liu Huan east to lecture for Ye; Jingchan invited Huan to his mountain dwelling to lecture on books, expending his entire fortune to host him; his son Qi personally put on sandals and served food to Huan's disciples — such was his courtesy to worthies.
translations.idiomatic: During Jianyuan, when the Prince of Wuling Ye was governor of Kuaiji, the Founding Emperor sent the Confucian Liu Huan east to lecture for Ye; Jingchan invited Huan to his mountain dwelling to lecture on books, expending his entire fortune to host him; his son Qi personally put on sandals and served food to Huan's disciples — such was his courtesy to worthies.

sentences.zh: 孔稚珪、周顒、謝蘥竝致書以通殷懃。

translations.literal: Kong Zhigui, Zhou Yong, and Xie Yue all sent letters to express warm regard.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Zhigui, Zhou Yong, and Xie Yue all sent letters to express warm regard.

sentences.zh: 永明十年，稚珪及光祿大夫陸澄、祠部尚書虞悰、太子右率沈約、司徒右長史張融表薦京產曰：「竊見吳郡杜京產，潔靜爲心，謙虛成性，通和發於天挺，敏達表於自然。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Yongming, Zhigui together with Palace Attendant Lu Cheng, Minister of Ceremonies Yu Song, Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Shen Yue, and Right Chief Secretary to the Grand Steward Zhang Rong submitted a memorial recommending Jingchan, saying: "We have observed Du Jingchan of Wu Commandery — purity and quietness form his heart, humility and modesty his nature; harmonious openness springs from Heaven's endowment, keen understanding shows in what is natural.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Yongming, Zhigui together with Palace Attendant Lu Cheng, Minister of Ceremonies Yu Song, Right Leader of the Heir Apparent's Household Shen Yue, and Right Chief Secretary to the Grand Steward Zhang Rong submitted a memorial recommending Jingchan, saying: "We have observed Du Jingchan of Wu Commandery — purity and quietness form his heart, humility and modesty his nature; harmonious openness springs from Heaven's endowment, keen understanding shows in what is natural.

sentences.zh: 學徧玄、儒，博通史、子，流連文藝，沈吟道奧。

translations.literal: His learning spans the arcane and Confucian; he broadly masters histories and masters; he lingers in literary arts and meditates on the Way's depths.
translations.idiomatic: His learning spans the arcane and Confucian; he broadly masters histories and philosophical works; he lingers in literary arts and meditates on the Way's depths.

sentences.zh: 泰始之朝，掛冠辭世，遁捨家業，隱于太平。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era he hung up his cap and withdrew from the world, abandoning family estate and hiding at Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era he hung up his cap and withdrew from the world, abandoning family estate and hiding at Taiping.

sentences.zh: 葺宇窮巖，採芝幽澗，耦耕自足，薪歌有餘。

translations.literal: He built a dwelling in remote cliffs, gathered fungus in hidden streams, paired-plowed for self-sufficiency, and had surplus for woodcutting songs.
translations.idiomatic: He built a dwelling in remote cliffs, gathered fungus in hidden streams, paired-plowed for self-sufficiency, and had surplus for woodcutting songs.

sentences.zh: 確爾不羣，淡然寡欲，麻衣藿食，二十餘載。

translations.literal: Steadfast and not of the crowd, plain and with few desires, hemp clothes and mallow food for more than twenty years.
translations.idiomatic: Steadfast and not of the crowd, plain and with few desires, he wore hemp clothes and ate mallow for more than twenty years.

sentences.zh: 雖古之志士，何以加之。

translations.literal: Even the aspiring worthies of antiquity — how could they surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: Even the aspiring worthies of antiquity — how could they surpass this?

sentences.zh: 謂宜釋巾幽谷，結組登朝，則喦谷含懽，薜蘿起抃矣。

translations.literal: We hold that he ought to cast off kerchief in the hidden valley and tie regalia to ascend court — then stream valleys would hold joy and rushes and moss would leap up [in delight].
translations.idiomatic: We hold that he ought to cast off his kerchief in the hidden valley and tie regalia to ascend court — then stream valleys would hold joy and rushes and moss would leap up in delight.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply was given.
translations.idiomatic: " No reply was given.

sentences.zh: 建武初，徵員外散騎侍郎，京產曰：「莊生持釣，豈爲白璧所回。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianwu, he was summoned as Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders; Jingchan said: "Master Zhuang held his fishing rod — how could he be turned by a white jade?
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Jianwu, he was summoned to serve as Extraordinary Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Loose Riders; Jingchan said: "Master Zhuang held his fishing rod — how could he be turned by a white jade?

sentences.zh: 」辭疾不就。

translations.literal: " He cited illness and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " He cited illness and declined.

sentences.zh: 年六十四，永元元年，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of sixty-four, in the first year of Yongyuan, he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of sixty-four, in the first year of Yongyuan, he died.

sentences.zh: 會稽孔道徵，守志業不仕，京產與之友善。

translations.literal: Kong Daozheng of Kuaiji kept to his resolve and did not take office; Jingchan was friendly with him.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Daozheng of Kuaiji kept to his resolve and did not take office; Jingchan was on friendly terms with him.

sentences.zh: 永明中，會稽鍾山有人姓蔡，不知名。

translations.literal: During Yongming, on Mount Zhong of Kuaiji there was a man surnamed Cai whose given name was unknown.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongming, on Mount Zhong in Kuaiji there was a man surnamed Cai whose given name was unknown.

sentences.zh: 山中養鼠數十頭，呼來卽來，遣去便去。

translations.literal: In the mountains he kept several dozen rats; when called they came, when sent away they went.
translations.idiomatic: In the mountains he kept several dozen rats; when called they came, when sent away they departed.

sentences.zh: 言語狂易，時謂之「謫仙」。

translations.literal: His speech was wild and erratic; the age called him "Banished Immortal."
translations.idiomatic: His speech was wild and erratic; his contemporaries called him "Banished Immortal."

sentences.zh: 不知所終。

translations.literal: No one knows how he ended.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows how he ended.

sentences.zh: 沈驎士

translations.literal: Shen Linshi
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linshi

sentences.zh: 沈驎士字雲禎，吳興武康人也。

translations.literal: Shen Linshi, courtesy name Yunzhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Linshi, courtesy name Yunzhen, was a native of Wukang in Wuxing Commandery.

sentences.zh: 祖膺期，晉太中大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yingqi was Jin Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yingqi served as Grand Master of the Palace under Jin.

sentences.zh: 驎士少好學，家貧，織簾誦書，口手不息。

translations.literal: Linshi from youth loved learning; his family was poor; he wove bamboo blinds and recited books, mouth and hand never ceasing.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Linshi loved learning; his family was poor; he wove bamboo blinds and recited books, mouth and hand never ceasing.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，文帝令尚書僕射何尚之抄撰五經，訪舉學士，縣以驎士應選。

translations.literal: Near the end of Yuanjia in Song, Emperor Wen ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat He Shangzhi to compile the Five Classics and to seek out and recommend scholars; the district recommended Linshi for selection.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Yuanjia era in Song, Emperor Wen ordered Vice Director of the Secretariat He Shangzhi to compile the Five Classics and to seek out and recommend scholars; the district recommended Linshi for selection.

sentences.zh: 尚之謂子偃曰：「山東故有奇士也。

translations.literal: Shangzhi said to his son Yan: "East of the mountains there truly are extraordinary men.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi said to his son Yan: "East of the mountains there truly are extraordinary men.

sentences.zh: 」少時，驎士稱疾歸郷，更不與人物通。

translations.literal: " After a short time, Linshi cited illness and returned to his home district, and no longer mingled with others.
translations.idiomatic: " After a short time, Linshi cited illness and returned to his home district, and no longer mingled with others.

sentences.zh: 養孤兄子，義著郷曲。

translations.literal: He raised his orphaned nephew; his righteousness was renowned in the district.
translations.idiomatic: He raised his orphaned nephew; his righteousness was renowned throughout the district.

sentences.zh: 或勸驎士仕，答曰：「魚縣獸檻，天下一契，聖人玄悟，所以每履吉先。

translations.literal: Some urged Linshi to take office; he replied: "Fish on the hook and beasts in the pen — under Heaven it is one bond; the sage darkly comprehends, and therefore each time treads auspicious ground first.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged Linshi to take office; he replied: "Fish on the hook and beasts in the pen — under Heaven it is one bond; the sage darkly comprehends, and therefore each time treads auspicious ground first.

sentences.zh: 吾誠未能景行坐忘，何爲不希企日損。

translations.literal: I truly cannot follow the good example and sit in forgetfulness — why should I not aspire to daily diminishment?"
translations.idiomatic: I truly cannot follow the good example and sit in forgetfulness — why should I not aspire to daily diminishment?"

sentences.zh: 」乃作《玄散賦》以絕世。

translations.literal: " He then composed the "Rhapsody on Mysterious Withdrawal" to break with the world.
translations.idiomatic: " He then composed the "Rhapsody on Mysterious Withdrawal" to break with the world.

sentences.zh: 太守孔山士辟，不應。

translations.literal: The Administrator Kong Shanshi summoned him; he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrator Kong Shanshi summoned him; he did not respond.

sentences.zh: 宗人徐州刺史曇慶、侍中懷文、左率勃來候之，驎士未嘗答也。

translations.literal: Clansmen — the Inspector of Xuzhou Tan Qing, Palace Attendant Huaiwen, and Left Leader Bo — came to visit him; Linshi never once responded.
translations.idiomatic: Clansmen — the Inspector of Xuzhou Tan Qing, Palace Attendant Huaiwen, and Left Leader Bo — came to visit him; Linshi never once responded.

sentences.zh: 隱居餘不吳差山，講經教授，從學者數十百人，各營屋宇，依止其側。

translations.literal: He lived in seclusion on Mount Wu Cha in Yubu, lecturing on the classics and teaching; those who came to study numbered several tens and hundreds, each building a dwelling and lodging at his side.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in seclusion on Mount Wu Cha in Yubu, lecturing on the classics and teaching; those who came to study numbered in the hundreds, each building a dwelling and lodging at his side.

sentences.zh: 驎士重陸機《連珠》，每爲諸生講之。

translations.literal: Linshi prized Lu Ji's Linked Pearls and regularly lectured on them for his students.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi prized Lu Ji's Linked Pearls and regularly lectured on them for his students.

sentences.zh: 征北張永爲吳興，請驎士入郡。

translations.literal: Zhang Yong, General Who Campaigns North, was governor of Wuxing and invited Linshi into the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yong, General Who Campaigns North, was governor of Wuxing and invited Linshi into the commandery.

sentences.zh: 驎士聞郡後堂有好山水，乃往停數月。

translations.literal: Linshi heard that behind the commandery hall there was fine landscape, and went to stay several months.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi heard that behind the commandery hall there was fine landscape, and went to stay several months.

sentences.zh: 永欲請爲功曹，使人致意。

translations.literal: Yong wished to invite him as Merit Officer and sent a messenger to convey his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yong wished to invite him to serve as Merit Officer and sent a messenger to convey his intent.

sentences.zh: 驎士曰：「明府德履沖素，留心山谷，民是以被褐負杖，忘其疲病。

translations.literal: Linshi said: "Your Excellency's virtue and conduct are pure and plain, your heart rests in mountains and valleys; for this reason this commoner wears coarse cloth and leans on his staff, forgetting his weariness and illness.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi said: "Your Excellency's virtue and conduct are pure and plain, your heart rests in mountains and valleys; for this reason this commoner wears coarse cloth and leans on his staff, forgetting his weariness and illness.

sentences.zh: 必欲飾渾沌以蛾眉，冠越客於文冕，走雖不敏，請附高節，有蹈東海而死爾。

translations.literal: If you must adorn Chaos with painted eyebrows and crown a Yue guest with an ornate cap, though I am not keen, I beg to attach myself to lofty integrity — there is only drowning in the Eastern Sea."
translations.idiomatic: If you must adorn Chaos with painted eyebrows and crown a Yue guest with an ornate cap, though I am not keen, I beg to attach myself to lofty integrity — there is only drowning in the Eastern Sea."

sentences.zh: 」永乃止。

translations.literal: " Yong then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: " Yong then stopped.

sentences.zh: 昇明末，太守王奐上表薦之，詔徵爲奉朝請，不就。

translations.literal: Near the end of the Shengming era, the Administrator Wang Huan submitted a memorial recommending him; an edict summoned him as Attendant at Court Audience; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Shengming era, the Administrator Wang Huan submitted a memorial recommending him; an edict summoned him to serve as Attendant at Court Audience; he declined.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，吏部郎沈淵、中書郎沈約又表薦驎士義行，曰：「吳興沈驎士，英風夙挺，峻節早樹，貞粹稟於天然，綜博生乎篤習。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming, Director of the Ministry of Personnel Shen Yuan and Secretariat Gentleman Shen Yue again submitted a memorial recommending Linshi's righteousness and conduct, saying: "Shen Linshi of Wuxing — heroic bearing sprang up early, lofty integrity was planted young; pure essence was endowed by nature, comprehensive breadth arose from devoted study.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Yongming, Director of the Ministry of Personnel Shen Yuan and Secretariat Gentleman Shen Yue again submitted a memorial recommending Linshi's righteousness and conduct, saying: "Shen Linshi of Wuxing — heroic bearing sprang up early, lofty integrity was planted young; pure essence was endowed by nature, comprehensive breadth arose from devoted study.

sentences.zh: 家世孤貧，藜藿不給，懷書而耕，白首無倦，挾琴採薪，行歌不輟。

translations.literal: His family for generations was solitary and poor; wild greens were insufficient; he carried books and plowed, white-haired yet never weary; with lute in arm he gathered firewood, walking and singing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: His family for generations was solitary and poor; wild greens were insufficient; he carried books and plowed, white-haired yet never weary; with lute in arm he gathered firewood, walking and singing without cease.

sentences.zh: 長兄早卒，孤姪數四，攝尪鞠稚，吞苦推甘。

translations.literal: His elder brother died early; he had four orphaned nephews; he cared for the weak and reared the young, swallowing bitterness and offering sweetness.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother died early; he had four orphaned nephews; he cared for the weak and reared the young, swallowing bitterness and offering sweetness.

sentences.zh: 年踰七十，業行無改。

translations.literal: Past seventy years, his conduct and practice were unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy years, his conduct and practice were unchanged.

sentences.zh: 元嘉以來，聘召仍疊，玉質踰潔，霜操日嚴。

translations.literal: Since Yuanjia, summons and invitations have piled up repeatedly; jade quality grows ever purer, frost integrity daily stricter.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Yuanjia era, summons and invitations have piled up repeatedly; jade quality grows ever purer, frost integrity daily stricter.

sentences.zh: 若使聞政王庭，服道槐掖，必能孚朝規於邊鄙，播聖澤於荒垂。

translations.literal: If he were to hear governance at the royal court and serve the Way in the palace side-chambers, he would surely be able to extend court norms to the borderlands and spread sage grace to remote regions.
translations.idiomatic: If he were to hear governance at the royal court and serve the Way in the palace side-chambers, he would surely extend court norms to the borderlands and spread sage grace to remote regions.

sentences.zh: 」詔又徵爲太學博士，建武二年，徵著作郎，永元二年，徵太子舍人，竝不就。

translations.literal: " An edict again summoned him as Erudite of the Grand Academy; in the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as Drafting Secretary; in the second year of Yongyuan he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent — all he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict again summoned him to serve as Erudite of the Grand Academy; in the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as Drafting Secretary; in the second year of Yongyuan he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent — he declined all.

sentences.zh: 驎士負薪汲水，幷日而食，守操終老。

translations.literal: Linshi carried firewood and drew water, eating every other day, keeping his resolve to the end of his life.
translations.idiomatic: Linshi carried firewood and drew water, eating every other day, keeping his resolve to the end of his life.

sentences.zh: 篤學不倦，遭火，燒書數千卷，驎士年過八十，耳目猶聦明，手以反故抄寫，火下細書，復成二三千卷，滿數十篋，時人以爲養身靜嘿之所致也。

translations.literal: Devoted to learning without weariness, he suffered a fire that burned several thousand scrolls of books; Linshi, past eighty, eyes and ears still keen, by hand copied on the reverse of old paper, writing fine script by lamplight, and again produced two or three thousand scrolls, filling several dozen cases; people of the time took this to result from nourishing the body in quiet silence.
translations.idiomatic: Devoted to learning without weariness, he suffered a fire that burned several thousand scrolls of books; Linshi, past eighty, eyes and ears still keen, copied by hand on the reverse of old paper, writing fine script by lamplight, and again produced two or three thousand scrolls, filling several dozen cases; people of the time took this to result from nourishing the body in quiet silence.

sentences.zh: 著《周易兩繫莊子內篇訓》，注《易經》、《禮記》、《春秋》、《尚書》、《論語》、《孝經》、《喪服》、《老子》要略數十卷。

translations.literal: He composed Exegesis on the Two Appended Sections of the Book of Changes and the Inner Chapters of the Zhuangzi, and annotated the Classic of Changes, Record of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, and Laozi — essential summaries in several tens of scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: He composed Exegesis on the Two Appended Sections of the Book of Changes and the Inner Chapters of the Zhuangzi, and annotated the Classic of Changes, Record of Rites, Spring and Autumn Annals, Documents, Analects, Classic of Filial Piety, Mourning Garments, and Laozi — essential summaries in several tens of scrolls.

sentences.zh: 以楊王孫、皇甫謐深達生死，而終禮矯偽，乃自作終制。

translations.literal: Because Yang Wangsun and Huangfu Mi deeply understood life and death yet ultimately observed rites that were forced and false, he himself composed his own final arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yang Wangsun and Huangfu Mi deeply understood life and death yet ultimately observed rites that were forced and false, he himself composed his own final arrangements.

sentences.zh: 年八十六，卒。

translations.literal: At the age of eighty-six, he died.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of eighty-six, he died.

sentences.zh: 同郡沈儼之，字士恭，徐州刺史曇慶子，亦不仕。

translations.literal: Shen Yanzhi of the same commandery, styled Shigong, was the son of Tanqing, Regional Inspector of Xuzhou; he likewise did not serve in office.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Yanzhi of the same commandery, courtesy name Shigong, was the son of Tanqing, Regional Inspector of Xuzhou; he too declined office.

sentences.zh: 徵太子洗馬，永明元年，徵中書郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household; in the first year of Yongming he was summoned as Secretariat Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to serve as Groom of the Heir Apparent's Household; in the first year of Yongming he was summoned as Secretariat Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 三年，又詔徵前南郡國常侍沈顗爲著作郎，建武二年，徵太子舍人，永元二年，徵通直郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, an edict again summoned the former Regular Attendant of the Principality of Nan Commandery, Shen Yi, as Drafting Secretary; in the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; in the second year of Yongyuan he was summoned as Attendant of Direct Communication.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, an edict again summoned the former Regular Attendant of the Principality of Nan Commandery, Shen Yi, to serve as Drafting Secretary; in the second year of Jianwu he was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary to the Heir Apparent; in the second year of Yongyuan he was summoned as Attendant of Direct Communication.

sentences.zh: 顗字處默，宋領軍寅之兄孫也。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Chumo, was the elder brother's grandson of Yin, General of the Household for the Song.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, courtesy name Chumo, was a grandson of the elder brother of Yin, General of the Household under Song.

sentences.zh: 魯國孔嗣之，字敬伯。

translations.literal: Kong Sizhi of Lu, styled Jingbo.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Sizhi of Lu, courtesy name Jingbo.

sentences.zh: 宋世與太祖俱爲中書舍人，竝非所好，自廬陵郡去官，隱居鍾山，朝廷以爲太中大夫。

translations.literal: In the Song era he and the Founding Emperor both served as Palace Attendants of the Secretariat; both were not to their liking; he resigned his post in Luling commandery, lived in seclusion on Mount Zhong, and the court made him Grand Master of the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he and the Founding Emperor had both served as Palace Attendants of the Secretariat; neither post suited him, so he resigned from Luling commandery, withdrew to Mount Zhong, and the court appointed him Grand Master of the Palace.

sentences.zh: 建武三年，卒。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianwu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 徐伯珍

translations.literal: Xu Bozhen
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bozhen

sentences.zh: 徐伯珍字文楚，東陽太末人也。

translations.literal: Xu Bozhen, styled Wenchu, was a native of Taimo in Dongyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Bozhen, courtesy name Wenchu, came from Taimo in Dongyang.

sentences.zh: 祖父竝郡掾史。

translations.literal: His grandfather and father both served as commandery clerks.
translations.idiomatic: Both his grandfather and his father had served as commandery clerks.

sentences.zh: 伯珍少孤貧，書竹葉及地學書。

translations.literal: Bozhen from youth was orphaned and poor; he wrote on bamboo leaves and on the ground to study writing.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned and poor from boyhood, Bozhen practiced writing on bamboo leaves and on the bare ground.

sentences.zh: 山水暴出，漂溺宅舍，村隣皆奔走，伯珍累牀而止，讀書不輟。

translations.literal: Mountain torrents suddenly burst forth, flooding and drowning the dwelling; neighbors all fled, but Bozhen piled up beds to stop the water and never ceased reading.
translations.idiomatic: When mountain floods suddenly burst forth and submerged his house, the neighbors all fled; Bozhen stacked beds to hold back the water and never stopped reading.

sentences.zh: 叔父璠之與顏延之友善，還祛蒙山立精舍講授，伯珍往從學，積十年，究尋經史，遊學者多依之。

translations.literal: His uncle Fanzhi was friendly with Yan Yanzhi; returning to Mount Meng he established a private academy to lecture and teach; Bozhen went to follow him in study; over ten years he exhaustively pursued the classics and histories, and many traveling scholars relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Fanzhi, a friend of Yan Yanzhi, returned to Mount Meng and built a private academy where he lectured; Bozhen went to study under him. After ten years he had thoroughly mastered the classics and histories, and many traveling scholars came to rely on him.

sentences.zh: 太守琅邪王曇生、吳郡張淹竝加禮辟，伯珍應召便退，如此者凡十二焉。

translations.literal: The Administrators Wang Tansheng of Langye and Zhang Yan of Wu both honored him with ceremonial invitations; Bozhen would answer the summons and then withdraw — this happened twelve times in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Administrators Wang Tansheng of Langye and Zhang Yan of Wu both honored him with formal invitations; Bozhen would answer each summons and then withdraw — twelve times in all.

sentences.zh: 徵士沈儼造膝談論，申以素交。

translations.literal: The recluse Shen Yi came knee-to-knee to discuss doctrine, reaffirming their old plain friendship.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Shen Yi would come to sit knee-to-knee with him in discussion, renewing their long-standing friendship.

sentences.zh: 吳郡顧歡擿出《尚書》滯義，伯珍訓答甚有條理，儒者宗之。

translations.literal: Gu Huan of Wu commandery raised obscure passages in the Documents; Bozhen's instruction and replies were very well ordered, and Confucian scholars took him as their model.
translations.idiomatic: When Gu Huan of Wu commandery raised obscure passages in the Documents, Bozhen's explanations were lucid and well ordered, and Confucian scholars looked to him as a master.

sentences.zh: 好釋氏、老莊，兼明道術，歲常旱，伯珍筮之，如期雨澍。

translations.literal: He was fond of Buddhism, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, and also understood Daoist arts; in years of constant drought, Bozhen would divine, and rain would come as scheduled.
translations.idiomatic: He was devoted to Buddhism, Laozi, and Zhuangzi, and also mastered Daoist arts; in years of persistent drought, Bozhen would perform divination, and rain would fall exactly as foretold.
