sentences.zh: 舉動有禮，過曲木之下，趨而避之。

translations.literal: His movements had propriety; passing beneath bent trees, he would hurry to avoid them.
translations.idiomatic: His every movement showed propriety; passing beneath a bent tree, he would quicken his step to avoid it.

sentences.zh: 早喪妻，晚不復重娶，自比曾參。

translations.literal: He lost his wife early; in old age he did not remarry, comparing himself to Zeng Shen.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his wife early and never remarried in his later years, taking himself as another Zeng Shen.

sentences.zh: 宅南九里有高山，班固謂之九巖山，後漢龍丘萇隱處也。

translations.literal: Nine li south of his dwelling was a high mountain that Ban Gu called Mount Jiuyan; it was the place where Longqiu Chang of Later Han had lived in seclusion.
translations.idiomatic: Nine li south of his home stood a high mountain that Ban Gu called Mount Jiuyan — the very place where Longqiu Chang of Later Han had withdrawn from the world.

sentences.zh: 山多龍鬚柏，望之五采，世呼爲婦人巖。

translations.literal: The mountain had many dragon-whisker cypresses; viewed from afar they showed five colors, and people of the age called it Lady's Cliff.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain was thick with dragon-whisker cypresses that, seen from a distance, shimmered in five colors; people called it Lady's Cliff.

sentences.zh: 二年，伯珍移居之。

translations.literal: In the second year, Bozhen moved there to live.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he moved his dwelling there.

sentences.zh: 門前生梓樹，一年便合抱。

translations.literal: Before his gate a catalpa tree sprang up; within one year it could be encircled with arms.
translations.idiomatic: A catalpa tree sprang up before his gate and within a year its trunk could be spanned by a man's arms.

sentences.zh: 館東石壁夜忽有赤光洞照，俄爾而滅。

translations.literal: On the stone cliff east of his lodge, at night red light suddenly shone through in illumination, and in a moment was extinguished.
translations.idiomatic: One night the stone cliff east of his lodge was suddenly pierced by red light; in an instant it vanished.

sentences.zh: 白雀一雙栖其戶牖，論者以爲隱德之感焉。

translations.literal: A pair of white magpies roosted at his doors and windows; commentators took this as a response to his hidden virtue.
translations.idiomatic: A pair of white magpies came to roost at his doors and windows; commentators took this as heaven's response to his hidden virtue.

sentences.zh: 永明二年，刺史豫章王辟議曹從事，不就。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongming, the Prince of Yuzhang, as Regional Inspector, invited him as Attendant in the Bureau of Deliberation; he did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongming, the Prince of Yuzhang, serving as Regional Inspector, invited him to serve as Attendant in the Bureau of Deliberation; he declined.

sentences.zh: 家甚貧窶，兄弟四人，皆白首相對，時人呼爲「四皓」。

translations.literal: His household was very poor and destitute; the four brothers, all white-haired, faced one another, and people of the time called them the "Four Ho."
translations.idiomatic: His household was desperately poor; all four brothers, white-haired, sat facing one another, and people called them the "Four Ho."

sentences.zh: 建武四年，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jianwu, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the fourth year of Jianwu.

sentences.zh: 年八十四。

translations.literal: He was eighty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was eighty-four.

sentences.zh: 受業生凡千餘人。

translations.literal: Students who received his instruction numbered more than a thousand in all.
translations.idiomatic: More than a thousand students had studied under him.

sentences.zh: 同郡樓幼瑜，亦儒學。

translations.literal: Lou Youyu of the same commandery was also a Confucian scholar.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Youyu of the same commandery was also a Confucian scholar.

sentences.zh: 著《禮捃遺》三十卷。

translations.literal: He composed thirty scrolls of Collected Remnants of Ritual.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote thirty scrolls of Collected Remnants of Ritual.

sentences.zh: 官至給事中。

translations.literal: In office he reached the post of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to the post of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 又同郡樓惠明，有道術。

translations.literal: Also Lou Huiming of the same commandery had mastery of the Way's arts.
translations.idiomatic: Also from the same commandery was Lou Huiming, a master of Daoist arts.

sentences.zh: 居金華山，禽獸毒螫者皆避之。

translations.literal: He dwelt on Mount Jinhua; beasts and venomous stingers all avoided him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived on Mount Jinhua, where even wild beasts and venomous creatures kept their distance.

sentences.zh: 宋明帝聞之，勑出住華林園，除奉朝請，固乞不受，求東歸。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Song heard of him and ordered him out to stay in Hualin Garden; he was appointed Attendant at Court Audience, but firmly begged not to accept and sought to return east.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming of Song heard of him, he ordered Huiming to come and stay in Hualin Garden and appointed him Attendant at Court Audience; Huiming firmly refused and begged to return east.

sentences.zh: 永明三年，忽乘輕舟向臨安縣，衆不知所以。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongming, he suddenly took a light boat toward Lin'an county; the crowd did not know why.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongming he suddenly took a light boat toward Lin'an county, and no one knew his reason.

sentences.zh: 尋而唐宇之賊破郡。

translations.literal: Soon afterward the bandits of Tang Yuzhi broke the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the rebel Tang Yuzhi overran the commandery.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子呼出住蔣山，又求歸，見許。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wenhu summoned him out to stay on Mount Jiang; he again sought to return, and permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wenhu summoned him to stay on Mount Jiang; he again asked to return home, and his request was granted.

sentences.zh: 世祖敕爲立館。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor ordered a lodge built for him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shizu ordered a lodge built for him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：顧歡論夷夏，優老而劣釋。

translations.literal: The historian says: In discussing barbarians and Chinese, Gu Huan favored Laozi and ranked Buddhism lower.
translations.idiomatic: The historian says: In his discussion of barbarian and Chinese teachings, Gu Huan favored Daoism and ranked Buddhism lower.

sentences.zh: 佛法者，理寂乎萬古，迹兆乎中世，淵源浩博，無始無邊，宇宙之所不知，數量之所不盡，盛乎哉！

translations.literal: The Buddha-dharma — its principle is silent through myriad ages, its traces manifest in the middle age; its sources vast and deep, without beginning or end; what the cosmos does not know, what reckoning cannot exhaust — how magnificent!
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha-dharma: its principle is still through all ages, its traces appear in the middle age; its source is vast and fathomless, without beginning or end — beyond what the cosmos knows, beyond what any reckoning can exhaust. How magnificent!

sentences.zh: 真大士之立言也。

translations.literal: This is the doctrine established by a true great being.
translations.idiomatic: Such is the teaching proclaimed by a true great being.

sentences.zh: 探機扣寂，有感必應，以大苞小，無細不容。

translations.literal: Probing the subtle and knocking on silence, whenever there is feeling there is response; the great embraces the small, nothing minute is excluded.
translations.idiomatic: It probes the hidden and knocks upon silence; where there is feeling, there is response; the great embraces the small, and nothing however minute lies outside it.

sentences.zh: 若乃儒家之教，仁義禮樂，仁愛義宜，禮從樂和而已；

translations.literal: As for Confucian teaching — benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music; benevolence is love, righteousness is propriety, rites derive from music's harmony — that is all;
translations.idiomatic: Confucian teaching speaks of benevolence, righteousness, rites, and music — love and propriety, rites arising from harmony — and that is all;

sentences.zh: 今則慈悲爲本，常樂爲宗，施舍惟機，低舉成敬。

translations.literal: now compassion is taken as root, eternal joy as foundation, giving according to circumstance, and humility and elevation alike become reverence.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism takes compassion as its root and eternal joy as its foundation, gives according to circumstance, and makes both humility and exaltation forms of reverence.

sentences.zh: 儒家之教，憲章祖述，引古證今，於學易悟；

translations.literal: Confucian teaching — statutes and ancestral transmission, citing antiquity to prove the present — is easy to grasp in study;
translations.idiomatic: Confucian teaching codifies ancestral doctrine and cites antiquity to illuminate the present — easy to grasp in study;

sentences.zh: 今樹以前因，報以後果，業行交酬，連璅相襲。

translations.literal: now causes are planted in former lives and effects reaped in later lives; karma and conduct reciprocate, linked chains succeeding one another.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism plants causes in former lives and reaps effects in later ones, with karma and conduct endlessly reciprocating in linked chains.

sentences.zh: 陰陽之教，占氣步景，授民以時，知其利害；

translations.literal: Yin-yang teaching — divining qi and pacing the sun's shadow, instructing the people in seasons, knowing benefit and harm;
translations.idiomatic: Yin-yang teaching divines qi and tracks the sun's shadow, teaching the people the seasons and discerning benefit and harm;

sentences.zh: 今則耳眼洞達，心智他通，身爲奎井，豈俟甘石。

translations.literal: now ears and eyes are penetrating, mind and spirit communicate with others, the body itself becomes the Dipper and Well — why wait for Gan and Shi's methods?
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism opens ears and eyes, joins mind and spirit to others, and makes the body itself the Dipper and Well — why wait upon the methods of Gan De and Shi Shen?

sentences.zh: 法家之教，出自刑理，禁姦止邪，明用賞罰；

translations.literal: Legalist teaching — arising from penal principles, forbidding wickedness and stopping evil, clearly applying reward and punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Legalist teaching springs from penal doctrine, forbidding wickedness and restraining evil through clear reward and punishment;

sentences.zh: 今則十惡所墜，五及無間，刀樹劔山，焦湯猛火，造受自貽，罔或差貳。

translations.literal: now the ten evils cause one to fall, the five punishments extend to Avici hell, knife-trees and sword-mountains, boiling cauldrons and fierce fire — creator and receiver bring it upon themselves, without any discrepancy.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism holds that the ten grave evils cast one down, that the five heinous crimes lead to uninterrupted hell, to knife-trees and sword-mountains, boiling cauldrons and raging fire — what one creates, one receives, without the slightest deviation.

sentences.zh: 墨家之教，遵上儉薄，磨踵滅頂，且猶非吝；

translations.literal: Mohist teaching — honoring above and practicing frugality, grinding heels and extinguishing crowns, yet still not stinting;
translations.idiomatic: Mohist teaching honors those above and practices frugality, wearing down heels and risking crown and life, yet still does not stint;

sentences.zh: 今則膚同斷瓠，目如井星，授子捐妻，在鷹庇鴿。

translations.literal: now skin is like a severed gourd, eyes like the Well constellation, sons are given away and wives abandoned, clutching hawk yet sheltering dove.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism demands skin hanging loose as a severed gourd, eyes deep as the Well constellation, the giving away of sons and abandonment of wives — clutching the hawk yet sheltering the dove.

sentences.zh: 從橫之教，所貴權謀，天口連環，歸乎適變；

translations.literal: Horizontal-and-vertical teaching — what it values is expedient stratagem, the heaven-sent mouth and linked rings, returning to apt adaptation;
translations.idiomatic: The strategists' teaching values expedient stratagem, the heaven-sent mouth and linked rings, and returns always to apt adaptation;

sentences.zh: 今則一音萬解，無待戶說，四辯三會，咸得吾師。

translations.literal: now one sound has myriad interpretations, with no need for door-to-door persuasion; the four eloquences and three assemblies — all may gain our master.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism gives myriad meanings to a single word, needs no door-to-door persuasion, and in the four eloquences and three assemblies all may find their teacher.

sentences.zh: 雜家之教，兼有儒墨；

translations.literal: Eclectic teaching combines Confucian and Mohist;
translations.idiomatic: Eclectic teaching combines Confucian and Mohist doctrines;

sentences.zh: 今則五時所宣，于何不盡。

translations.literal: now what the five periods proclaim — what is not fully covered?
translations.idiomatic: whereas what the five periods of the Buddha's teaching proclaim — what is not fully encompassed?

sentences.zh: 農家之教，播植耕耘，善相五事，以藝九穀；

translations.literal: Agrarian teaching — sowing, planting, cultivating, and plowing, skilled in the five affairs, through craft producing the nine grains;
translations.idiomatic: Agrarian teaching teaches sowing, planting, cultivation, and plowing, skilled management of the five affairs, and the cultivation of the nine grains;

sentences.zh: 今則鬱單梗稻，已異閻浮，生天果報，自然飲良。

translations.literal: now the rice stalks of Uttarakuru already differ from Jambudvipa; birth in heaven and karmic fruit ripen naturally in fine nourishment.
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism speaks of Uttarakuru's rice stalks unlike those of Jambudvipa, of rebirth in heaven and karmic fruit, and of feasting naturally upon the finest fare.

sentences.zh: 道家之教，執一虛無，得性亡情，凝神勿擾；

translations.literal: Daoist teaching — holding to the One and emptiness, attaining nature and forgetting feelings, concentrating spirit without disturbance;
translations.idiomatic: Daoist teaching holds to the One and to emptiness, attains nature and forgets emotion, and concentrates the spirit without disturbance;

sentences.zh: 今則波若無照，萬法皆空，豈有道之可名，寧餘一之可得。

translations.literal: now prajna has no fixed illumination, myriad dharmas all are empty — how can the Way be named? How can one more "One" be obtained?
translations.idiomatic: whereas Buddhism holds that prajna has no fixed illumination, that myriad dharmas are all empty — how then can the Way be named? How can even one more "One" be grasped?

sentences.zh: 道俗對校，真假將讎，釋理奧藏，無往而不有也。

translations.literal: When Dao and lay teachings are compared, true and false will contend; Buddhist doctrine's profound treasury — there is nowhere it is not present.
translations.idiomatic: Set Daoist and lay teachings side by side, and truth and falsehood must contend; Buddhist doctrine's profound treasury is present everywhere one turns.

sentences.zh: 能善用之，卽真是俗。

translations.literal: If one can use it well, then truth and the secular are one.
translations.idiomatic: Used well, truth and the secular become one.

sentences.zh: 九流之設，用藉世教，刑名道墨，乖心異旨，儒者不學，無傷爲儒；

translations.literal: The establishment of the Nine Schools served to lend worldly teaching; Legalism, Names, Daoism, and Mohism — minds divergent, aims different; a Confucian need not study them, no harm to being Confucian;
translations.idiomatic: The Nine Schools were established to serve worldly instruction; Legalism, Names, Daoism, and Mohism differ in mind and aim — a Confucian need not study them and still remain a Confucian;

sentences.zh: 佛理玄曠，實智妙有，一物不知，不成圓聖。

translations.literal: Buddhist principle is vast and remote, real wisdom and subtle existence — not knowing one thing, one cannot become a perfect sage.
translations.idiomatic: but Buddhist principle is vast and profound, its real wisdom and subtle existence such that not to know one thing is not to become a perfect sage.

sentences.zh: 若夫神道應現之力，感會變化之奇，不可思議，難用言象。

translations.literal: As for the divine Way's power of responsive manifestation, the marvel of sympathetic transformation — inconceivable, hard to express in words and images.
translations.idiomatic: As for the divine Way's power of responsive manifestation and the marvel of sympathetic transformation — these are inconceivable and cannot be conveyed in words or images.

sentences.zh: 而諸張米道，符水先驗，相傳師法，祖自伯陽。

translations.literal: Yet the various Zhang rice-Dao lineages — talisman-water has prior verification, master-disciple dharma is transmitted, ancestry traced from Boyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the various Zhang rice-Dao lineages offer talisman-water with proven effect, transmit master-disciple doctrine, and trace their ancestry to Boyang.

sentences.zh: 世情去就，有此二學，僧尼道士，矛楯相非。

translations.literal: Worldly sentiment in approach and withdrawal has these two teachings; monks, nuns, and Daoist priests oppose one another with spear and shield.
translations.idiomatic: In worldly choice between the two teachings, monks and nuns and Daoist priests oppose one another like spear against shield.

sentences.zh: 非唯重道，兼亦殉利。

translations.literal: Not only do they cherish the Way; they also pursue profit.
translations.idiomatic: They cherish the Way, but they also pursue profit.

sentences.zh: 詳尋兩教，理歸一極。

translations.literal: Examining both teachings in detail, principle returns to one ultimate.
translations.idiomatic: Examined closely, both teachings return to one ultimate principle.

sentences.zh: 但迹有左右，故教成先後。

translations.literal: But traces have left and right, so teachings form earlier and later.
translations.idiomatic: Yet their traces diverge to left and right, and so their teachings arose earlier and later.

sentences.zh: 廣略爲言，自生優劣。

translations.literal: Broad and narrow in expression, superiority and inferiority arise of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Stated broadly or narrowly, superiority and inferiority arise of themselves.

sentences.zh: 道本虛無，非由學至，絕聖棄智，已成有爲。

translations.literal: Dao's root is emptiness and non-being, not reached through study; "abandon sages and discard wisdom" is already becoming purposeful action.
translations.idiomatic: Dao's root is emptiness and non-being, not attained through study; to "abandon sages and discard wisdom" is already to become purposeful action.

sentences.zh: 有爲之無，終非道本。

translations.literal: Non-being that is purposeful action — ultimately is not Dao's root.
translations.idiomatic: Non-being pursued through purposeful action is ultimately not Dao's root.

sentences.zh: 若使本末同無，曾何等級。

translations.literal: If root and branch were equally non-being, what grade would there be between them?
translations.idiomatic: If root and branch were equally non-being, what distinction of rank could there be?

sentences.zh: 佛則不然，具縛爲種，轉暗成明，梯愚入聖。

translations.literal: The Buddha is not so; bound with all fetters as seed, turning darkness into light, climbing from folly into sagehood.
translations.idiomatic: The Buddha is not so: he takes full bondage as seed, turns darkness into light, and climbs from folly into sagehood.

sentences.zh: 途雖遠而可踐，業雖曠而有期。

translations.literal: The path though distant can be tread; karma though vast has its term.
translations.idiomatic: The path, though distant, can be walked; karma, though vast, has its term.

sentences.zh: 勸慕之道，物我無隔。

translations.literal: The Way of exhortation and aspiration — self and things without barrier.
translations.idiomatic: In the Way of exhortation and aspiration, self and things are not divided.

sentences.zh: 而局情淺智，鮮能勝受。

translations.literal: Yet narrow sentiment and shallow wisdom — few can triumphantly receive it.
translations.idiomatic: Yet narrow feeling and shallow wisdom can rarely receive it fully.

sentences.zh: 世途揆度，因果二門。

translations.literal: The world's path measured, cause and effect are two gates.
translations.idiomatic: Measured by the world's path, cause and effect seem two separate gates.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴爲善，未必餘慶；

translations.literal: Doing good from the rooster's crow does not necessarily bring surplus blessing;
translations.idiomatic: Doing good from cockcrow does not necessarily bring surplus blessing;

sentences.zh: 膾肉東陵，曾無厄禍。

translations.literal: Sliced meat at Dongling — never met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: minced meat at Dongling never brought disaster in turn.

sentences.zh: 身才高妙，鬱滯而靡達；

translations.literal: Persons of high talent and refinement are blocked and do not reach fulfillment;
translations.idiomatic: Men of lofty talent and refinement languish without advancement;

sentences.zh: 器思庸鹵，富厚以終生。

translations.literal: Minds coarse and dull enjoy wealth and plenty to life's end.
translations.idiomatic: while coarse and dull minds live out their days in wealth and plenty.

sentences.zh: 忠反見遺；

translations.literal: Loyalty is instead abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: Loyalty is cast aside;

sentences.zh: 詭乃獲用。

translations.literal: Cunning then obtains employment.
translations.idiomatic: while cunning wins employment.

sentences.zh: 觀此而論，近無罪福，而業有不定，著自經文，三報開宗，斯疑頓曉。

translations.literal: Viewing this and arguing, in the near term there seems no guilt or fortune, yet karma is not fixed — established in the sutras, the three retributions open the doctrine, and this doubt is instantly clarified.
translations.idiomatic: Judged by this, reward and retribution seem absent in the near term; yet karma is not fixed — as the sutras establish, the doctrine of the three retributions opens the teaching, and this doubt is instantly resolved.

sentences.zh: 史臣服膺釋氏，深信冥緣，謂斯道之莫貴也。

translations.literal: The historian submits to the Buddha's teaching, deeply believes in hidden karmic affinity, and deems this Way nothing more precious.
translations.idiomatic: The historian submits to Buddhism, deeply believes in hidden karmic affinity, and holds this Way to be beyond price.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：含貞抱樸，履道敦學。

translations.literal: Eulogy: Embracing purity and holding simplicity, treading the Way and earnest in learning.
translations.idiomatic: Eulogy: Holding fast to integrity and plainness, walking the Way with earnest devotion to learning.

sentences.zh: 惟茲潛隱，棄鱗養角。

translations.literal: Only these hidden ones, discarding scales and nurturing horns.
translations.idiomatic: Only these hidden ones, shedding their scales and nurturing their horns.

translations.literal: Footnote marker in the source text.
translations.idiomatic: Editorial footnote marker in the source.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七二年一月版《南齊書》爲本校。

translations.literal: The full text uses the January 1972 Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi as the collation standard.
translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the January 1972 Zhonghua Shuju edition of the Book of Southern Qi.
